item.title: 0 key passes, 0 dribbles, 25% duels won: Youri Tielemans continues to flatter to deceive in Man United colours
item.description: 0 key passes, 0 dribbles, 25% duels won: Youri Tielemans continues to flatter to deceive in Man United colours Manchester United’s season hit a new low on Sunday afternoon. The match The Red Devils were convincingly beaten 0-3 by AFC Bournemouth, with little to no fight shown. Two goals in the first half and one in the second half were enough to vanquish United. Old Trafford was sympathetic to manager Michael Carrick but let their wrath be felt against the owners, football hierarchy, and players on an afternoon of discontent. Youri Tielemans The Belgian arrived at the club with a big reputation, having scored in the Europa League final and having been a key player for Aston Villa over the years. Capturing the midfielder for just £35 million was also seen as a major coup. Nonetheless, Tielemans’ impact has been nothing like what the supporters of the club would have hoped for this season. The Belgian was substituted at half-time and replaced by Matheus Cunha after another poor match. He had zero key passes in the match and did not connect with any of his crosses. Tielemans also completed just 14 passes in the match and did not take any shots at goal, as he carried little to no threat going forward. The experienced man in the middle of the park also did not win any tackles or complete any dribbles for his side. He was also exceedingly weak in his duels, winning just two out of nine ground battles and only one of three aerial duels. Tielemans will need to improve massively over the next few weeks if he is to justify why United brought him in this summer. His next chance will be when the Red Devils travel to Stamford Bridge to face Chelsea this Saturday, which falls on Halloween. vs AFC Bournemouth Featured image by Dan Istitene via Getty Images

item.title: Texans’ Tank Dell sums up long-awaited return with powerful message
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Texans’ Tank Dell sums up long-awaited return with powerful message appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Texans welcomed wide receiver Tank Dell back onto the field on Sunday. Dell has been sidelined for nearly two years after suffering a devastating knee injury in December 2024. On Sunday, he finally got back onto the field for game action. The Texans were unable to deliver a win for their returning wide receiver. Houston lost a close game to JJ McCarthy and the New York Giants. Dell had one catch, which went for 43 yards. It was his only target in this contest. After the game, Dell reflected on his return to the NFL. “I’m blessed. I feel blessed, but not really a relief. I’m grateful for everything, but I’m a playmaker. I’m so used to making those plays and there are so many more to come,” the Texans star said, via KPRC 2 Houston reporter Aaron Wilson. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Houston’s offense wasn’t all that effective in this loss. Tight end Dalton Schultz led the team with 45 yards receiving on Sunday. Houston managed just 237 yards of offense in this game as well. But the Texans’ strong defense kept them in this one. Despite giving up over 400 yards of offense, they picked up some crucial stops. In the end, it wasn’t enough, and the Giants pulled away with a huge win. The Texans are now 2-4 on the season, and their playoff chances are starting to feel like a longshot. With Dell healthy, this could certainly change. Hopefully he remains healthy and can be a productive part of this offense for years to come. Related: DeMeco Ryans rips ‘ridiculous’ penalty woes that keep costing Texans games Related: Tank Dell is back, but Marvin Harrison Jr. steals show with first Texans TD

item.title: Why Mike Tomlin believes Lions’ Dan Campbell made right 4th down decision vs. Packers
item.description: Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Why Mike Tomlin believes Lions’ Dan Campbell made right 4th down decision vs. Packers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Lions are 4-2 on the 2026-27 NFL season after Dan Campbell ’s team responded from a failed fourth down gamble to force a missed Green Bay Packers field goal, and to drive down for a game-winning Jake Bates kick . Running back Jahmyr Gibbs, who was stopped on the fourth down play, had a NSFW reaction to Campbell’s gutsy call while NBC commentator Mike Tomlin also shared his thoughts. Tomlin spoke with Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth of NBC, during which he saw things from Campbell’s point-of-view . “It centers around elite quarterback play, when you’ve got elite quarterback play, you want to make sure your guy at least has a chance to have the ball at the end of that game. If he punts that ball the way Jordan Love and company have been operating, it’s not possible, it’s probable, that they’re gonna matriculate the ball down the field and win the game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “And so what (Campbell) did by going for it, he was either gonna be successful and keep the ball for his quarterback, or he was gonna at least give his quarterback a chance to answer.” Tomlin said he used to prepare for such scenarios when he had Ben Roethlisberger as his quarterback in Pittsburgh as head coach of the Steelers. The Lions celebrated like champions during the Packers game, and are full of spirit headed toward the midway point of the season. They have little time to rest on their laurels with coach Kevin O’Connell’s Minnesota Vikings headed to Motown on Nov. 1, a game the Lions could find themselves as underdogs in, especially after their close shave against the Packers. Related: Lions’ Jahmyr Gibbs reveals NSFW reaction to Dan Campbell’s decision vs. Packers Related: Lions’ Brian Branch reacts to massive INT in injury return

item.title: 'No one cried before the match!' – Jose Mourinho hails hero Andriy Lunin after El Clasico masterclass
item.description: FC Barcelona v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Real Madrid goalkeeper Andriy Lunin delivered a superb performance in place of Thibaut Courtois, producing a miraculous save to help secure a 2-1 El Clasico win over Barcelona. Both Jose Mourinho and captain Fede Valverde singled out the Ukrainian for his daily professionalism. Lunin steps up on biggest stage to deny Barcelona Andriy Lunin delivered a memorable goalkeeping display as Real Madrid claimed a 2-1 victory over Barcelona at the Camp Nou. Replacing the injured Thibaut Courtois, the Ukrainian goalkeeper made several vital interventions to preserve Madrid's lead. His standout moment arrived in the 66th minute, pulling off a prodigious save to deny Gerard Martin's point-blank header from a corner. Lunin's composure ensured Real Madrid collected all three points away from home. Mourinho and Valverde praise goalkeeper's preparation Post-match, Jose Mourinho praised Lunin's mindset coming off the bench . "The only thing I told Lunin before the match was, ‘You train to play, not to sit on the bench. Go and play,’" Mourinho revealed. "He played a very balanced and composed match... none of us cried before the match because Thibaut wasn’t playing." Captain Fede Valverde added: "There are no words to describe what he did today... He's always working behind the scenes, giving his all." Ukrainian stopper reveals secret behind crucial saves Speaking after the match, Lunin credited his daily work with goalkeeping coach Nuno for his sharpness under pressure. "Discipline and attitude were key because Barcelona had more possession," Lunin explained. "Nuno always says 'well trained' and I think it's because of the daily work." "When the game is difficult... you have to know how to suffer, manage the game and be a team until the end," he added. Lunin reinforces Los Blancos' goalkeeping strength Lunin's stellar display once again highlighted Real Madrid's exceptional goalkeeping depth in major fixtures. The Ukrainian remains ready whenever called upon by Mourinho during Courtois' recovery. Real Madrid look forward to their next La Liga outing against Santander.

item.title: Darius Acuff Jr. passes Jason Williams on Kings’ all-time list
item.description: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Darius Acuff Jr. passes Jason Williams on Kings’ all-time list appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Sacramento Kings are still searching for their first win in the early-goings of the 2026-27 season, but rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. has been a major bright spot. Despite the Kings’ most recent loss, 123-113 to the Memphis Grizzlies, Acuff had another big game, surpassing former Kings guard Jason Williams for third most points through three games as a rookie, as per Kings on NBCS. With 22 points against the Grizzlies, Darius Acuff Jr. has a total of 67 points through the first three games of his Kings career, trailing only Maurice Stokes and Oscar Robertson, respectively. Stoke had 75 points through his first three games and Robertson had 72. Jason Williams is now in fourth place on the list with 56 points. The No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Acuff spent one season at Arkansas before declaring for the draft. His stoke rose throughout his lone year with the Razorbacks to where he was a sure lottery pick coming into the draft. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Through the first two games of his NBA career, Acuff has been averaging 22.5 points, 2.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.5 steals with splits of 30 percent shooting from the field, 11.1 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 76.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line. Obviously the shooting percentages raise eyebrows, but there isn’t any questioning the talent. And against the Grizzlies, Acuff had 22 points in 36 minutes while shooting 9-of-23 from the field, 2-of-9 from the 3-point line and 2-of-2 from the free-throw line. He also added three rebounds, seven assists and one blocked shot. He only had one turnover as well. The shooting percentages are still a concern, but it does look like the Kings got a great building block for the future. Related: Zach LaVine points out issue amid Kings’ 0-3 start to 2026 season Related: Grizzlies vs. Kings injury report: Zach Edey, Cedric Coward, Keegan Murray all listed

item.title: Ranking the 6 worst trades in WNBA history, from Becky Hammon to Angel Reese
item.description: Ranking the 6 worst trades in WNBA history, from Becky Hammon to Angel Reese originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Like all North American sports league, the WNBA's history is awash with baffling roster moves. Even the most astute franchises can get things wrong every now and then. In 2010, the Liberty sold low on a first-round pick, sending it to the Sparks in exchange for some immediate help. That transaction set into motion a chain of events that ended with the Sun acquiring future MVP Tina Charles and the Lynx landing future Basketball Hall of Famer Lindsay Whalen. Trades, like draft picks, are only as effective as the franchises that facilitate them. On occasion, the calculus that one team employs to land another piece skews away from its desired result. The consequences can set an organization back decades. With that, here's a look back at the worst trades in WNBA history. MORE: How Dream's arena upgrade saved the WNBA from an eyesore Ranking worst trades in WNBA history Imagn Images 6. Ariel Atkins for rights to Sonia Citron, 2025 Sky receive: Ariel Atkins Mystics receive: Rights to Sonia Citron, 2027 first-round pick swap, 2027 second-round pick The Sky hoped to accelerate their rebuild after dour showings during the 2023 and 2024 campaigns. They opted to part way with draft capital to do so, sending the No. 3 pick in the 2025 draft to Washington in exchange for two-time All-Star Ariel Atkins. Atkins, a former five-time All-Defensive selection, figured to bring the versatility that Tyler Marsh's side craved. The experiment lasted little more than a year; Atkins was shipped to the Sparks in April 2026. Washington, meanwhile, used its newly-acquired pick to select Sonia Citron. The Notre Dame product has enjoyed a sterling start to life in the WNBA, earning two All-Star appearances thus far. The deal could prove even more lopsided in the Mystics' favor come April; the Mystics will acquire Chicago's top-four-bound pick in next year's draft via pick swap. 5. Kristi Toliver for Angie Bjorklund, 2010 Sparks receive: Kristi Toliver Sky receive: Rights to Angie Bjorklund Los Angeles was in the midst of an underwhelming run when it made a move for Toliver, the Sky's No. 3 pick in the 2009 Draft. The Maryland product showed flashes of her three-point prowess during her lone season with Chicago, placing second in the league in three-point shooting. Despite her penchant for triples, Toliver was deemed surplus to requirements by Chicago's front office. The Sparks were the beneficiary if that mischaracterization, acquiring Toliver in exchange for their 2011 second-round pick. Bjorklund, the player the Sky selected with Los Angeles' pick, played seven games in the WNBA. Toliver, meanwhile, earned three All-Star appearances, two titles and the 2012 Most Improved Player prize. MORE: Three details you missed about Angel Reese's shoes 4. Kelsey Plum for rights to Dominique Malonga, 2025 Spa
item.content:encoded: Ranking the 6 worst trades in WNBA history, from Becky Hammon to Angel Reese originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Like all North American sports league, the WNBA's history is awash with baffling roster moves. MORE: How Dream's arena upgrade saved the WNBA from an eyesore Ranking worst trades in WNBA history Imagn Images 6. The Notre Dame product has enjoyed a sterling start to life in the WNBA, earning two All-Star appearances thus far. The deal could prove even more lopsided in the Mystics' favor come April; the Mystics will acquire Chicago's top-four-bound pick in next year's draft via pick swap. 5. Kristi Toliver for Angie Bjorklund, 2010 Sparks receive: Kristi Toliver Sky receive: Rights to Angie Bjorklund Los Angeles was in the midst of an underwhelming run when it made a move for Toliver, the Sky's No. 3 pick in the 2009 Draft. The Maryland product showed flashes of her three-point prowess during her lone season with Chicago, placing second in the league in three-point shooting. Despite her penchant for triples, Toliver was deemed surplus to requirements by Chicago's front office. The Sparks were the beneficiary if that mischaracterization, acquiring Toliver in exchange for their 2011 second-round pick. Bjorklund, the player the Sky selected with Los Angeles' pick, played seven games in the WNBA. Toliver, meanwhile, earned three All-Star appearances, two titles and the 2012 Most Improved Player prize. MORE: Three details you missed about Angel Reese's shoes 4. Kelsey Plum for rights to Dominique Malonga, 2025 Sparks receive: Kelsey Plum, rights to Sarah Ashlee Barker, rights to Chance Gray Aces receive: Jewell Loyd, rights to Aaliyah Nye Storm receive: Rights to Dominique Malonga, Li Yueru, rights to Taina Mair After failing to make the playoffs in five straight seasons, the Sparks attempted to make a splash acquisition during the 2025 offseason. Los Angeles acquired Kelsey Plum in a three-team blockbuster with the Aces and Storm, sending the rights to its first-round pick to Seattle in the deal. The move proved a curious one at the time. The Sparks needed talent, to be sure. But with Cameron Brink and Rickea Jackson already in town, they seemed better suited to continue to prioritize their youth. Instead, Los Angeles mortgaged its future. Plum performed admirably in Sparks colors, averaging 20.5 points and 5.9 assists across 55 appearances for L.A. Unfortunately for Los Angeles, Plum's displays did little to improve its standing. She skipped town a little more than a year after arriving, made the centerpiece of a trade deadline swap to the Mercury. That No. 2 pick would come back to cost the Sparks. Seattle selected French big Dominique Malonga with Los Angeles' selection. She became the youngest player to earn an All-Star selection in 2026 and figures to be one of the sport's brightest supernovas for years to come. 3. Katie Smith for Chandi Jones, Stacey Thomas, rights to Shona Thorburn, 2005 Shock receive: Katie Smith Lynx receive: Chandi Jones, Stacey Thomas, rights to Shona Thorburn Smith was Minnesota's best player in its first years of existence, picking up MVP votes every season from 2000-06. She saw her numbers tumble in by the mid-point of the 2005 season. At 31, she appeared to be in the midst of her prime. But underwhelming returns in the first half of the season prompted the Lynx to dangle her to consider sending her elsewhere. Detroit benefitted from Minnesota's decision, landing Smith for a cut-rate fee in the form of Jones, Thomas and a 2006 first-rounder. The Basketball Hall of Famer went on to play eight more seasons in the league, accruing two more All-Star berths with the Shock. She also helped power two title-winning Detroit sides, capturing Finals MVP honors for her efforts during the 2008 championship series. Smith was elected to the Basketball Hall of Fame in 2018. Jones, Thomas and Thorburn combined to play 29 games for the Lynx. 2. Angel Reese for 2027, 2028 first round picks Dream receive: Angel Reese, 2028 second-round pick swap Sky receive: 2027 first-round pick, 2028 first-round pick Chicago opted out of the Reese experiment after just two seasons, sending her to the Dream in exchange for two first-round picks — both of which are likely to be near the bottom of the board. While there were certain parts of Reese's game that undoubtedly needed refinement upon her Sky exit, she was a two-time All-Star who already established herself as the sport's greatest-ever rebounder (and one of its premier defenders, too). The franchise worked with Reese to manufacture the move to her preferred destination, an act of goodwill amid a fracturing relationship between employee and employer. Reese's departure confirmed that the franchise held 6-7 big Kamilla Cardoso — drafted four spots before the LSU product in the 2024 Draft — in higher regard than Reese. It hasn't even been a year, yet that assessment already looks to be a disastrous one. The Sky toiled in 2026, winning just16 games. Reese, meanwhile, picked up Defensive Player of the Year and All-WNBA second team honors. She was a pillar on Atlanta's roster as it raced to its third-ever WNBA Finals, producing memorable numbers as the Dream locked horns with the Valkyries. Perhaps the Sky can salvage some of the damage by making astute selections with Atlanta's 2027 and 2028 firsts. But at present, it's hard to argue against the idea of this trade being one of the worst in league history. Chicago won't even get anything out of its lackluster displays, having surrender its 2027 and 2028 first-rounders to the Mystics. 1. Becky Hammon for Jessica Davenport, 2007 Silver Stars receive: Becky Hammon, rights to Chioma Nmamaka Liberty receive: Jessica Davenport, rights to Erlana Larkins We flirted with giving Reese top billing on this list, considering the shock value of her departure given her age, production and marketability to Chicago (and now, Atlanta's) franchise. In the end, it's still too soon to brandish her with the crown. Hammon's trade remains the measuring stick by which other heists are compared to. It's easy to see why. New York was well-aware of Hammon's gifts when it sent her packing. She was a three-time All-Star who earned All-WNBA second team honors in her penultimate season in Liberty colors. Hammon immediately became San Antonio's most important player, finishing second in MVP honors in her maiden 2008 campaign with the franchise. She would go on to make three All-WNBA teams during her time with the Silver Sta

item.title: Nepal Premier League prize money: How much will teams, players earn for winning NPL 2026?
item.description: The third season of the Nepal Premier League begins on October 26 at the Tribhuvan University International Cricket Ground in Kirtipur, with eight franchises in the fray. The Cricket Association of Nepal has raised the prize pot considerably for this edition, with the champions now due to collect NPR 15 million, up from the NPR 10 million paid out in each of the first two seasons. MAKE YOUR BET WITH DAFABET AND GET UP TO 200% WELCOME BONUS Janakpur Bolts won the inaugural title in 2024, and Lumbini Lions are the defending champions. Add The Sporting News as a preferred news source NPL 2026 prize money breakdown CAN confirmed the figures at a press conference on the eve of the tournament. The top four finishers all collect a share, with the gap between first and second now worth NPR 7 million. Position Prize money (NPR) Winners 15,000,000 Runners-up 8,000,000 Third place 4,000,000 Fourth place 3,000,000 The rise is being funded by what CAN expects to be a far bigger commercial return than in previous seasons. Treasurer Padam Khadka put the projected gross revenue for the month-long tournament at NPR 1.5 billion. The board is anticipating NPR 200 million from sponsorships and more than NPR 700 million from ticketing and broadcasting combined. "As a result, the prize money has also been increased," Khadka said, linking the two directly. item.title: CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen confirms Bayern delegation for Ballon d’Or gala
item.description: (Photo by S. Stingl/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images Bayern Munich CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen has confirmed that the club will send an official delegation to London for Monday’s Ballon d’Or ceremony, expressing optimism as the Bavarian giants boast their highest number of individual and club nominations in a decade. Leading the accolades for Bayern is Harry Kane, whom Dreesen labeled a “360-degree striker” in an interview captured by @iMiaSanMia . “We would, of course, be absolutely delighted if Harry Kane were to win the Ballon d’Or. Harry sets new records year after year, but his 73 goals for FC Bayern and the England national team carry particular significance this time around. I like to call him our ‘360-degree striker’ because he always has the entire pitch in view, works tirelessly and makes his teammates better. He has continued to develop his game and, in doing so, has transformed our entire team’s style of play. He is a global superstar without any airs and graces, while also being a gentleman who sets an outstanding example both on and off the pitch,” said the CEO. Beyond Kane, Dreesen also singled out French winger Michael Olise as a future Ballon d’Or recipient, marking a milestone year where four Bayern players feature on the m en’s 30-man shortlist for the first time in ten years. “Michael Olise also thoroughly deserves his place on the shortlist, and I a m convinced that he, too, will win the Ballon d’Or one day. Overall, our many nominations are a wonderful recognition o f a fantastic season. For the first time in ten years, four FC Bayern players are once again on the Ba llon d’Or shortlist . On top of that, Vincent Kompany is recognized as one of the best coaches in the world, and for the first time, both our women’s and men’s teams have been nominated for Club of the Year. Naturally, we will tra vel to London with all due humility, hoping that we will also have the opportunity to celebrate a few awards,” he said . Coupled with Vincent Kompany’s nomination for Coach of the Year and historical, simultaneous Club of the Year nominations fo r both the FC Bayern men’s and women’s teams, the club heads to London ready to celebrate an exceptional campaign. Do you think Harry Kane’s 73-goal season makes him the undisputed favorite to lift the Ball on d’Or in London? Let us know in the comments! Key Corrections Made:

item.title: Seahawks’ Mike Macdonald sees turning point after SNF Chiefs blowout
item.description: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images Seahawks’ Mike Macdonald sees turning point after SNF Chiefs blowout appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Seattle Seahawks ended the Kansas City Chiefs’ unbeaten season in what is easily their biggest win in their title defense to date. Their defense stepped up in a big way, shutting down Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs offense in a 20-3 blowout win on Sunday Night Football. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald expressed pride at his team’s performance amid some early-season adversity and is hoping this win can be a launching pad for their season. “There’s a sense of urgency now to take another step as a football team,” Macdonald said post-game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The much-hyped revenge game featuring Walker III, who left Seattle this offseason, turned into a one-sided affair in favor of the Seahawks. They limited the reigning Super Bowl MVP to by far his least productive rushing game of the season with just 36 yards on 14 carries. Patrick Mahomes was also held to his lowest passing output of the season with only 165 yards. He also went without a touchdown pass for the second straight game. As for the Seahawks offense, quarterback Sam Darnold had a solid performance. He completed a season-best 71 percent of his passes for 257 yards and a touchdown with one interception. Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba played his part in helping Darnold with nine catches for 150 yards and a score. He also made some history with his amazing start to the season . Despite being 4-3, this is the type of all-around performance the Seahawks are capable of, which still makes them a dangerous team. But another big test is coming up for them as they host the 5-2 Chicago Bears next week on Monday night. Related: Seahawks’ Nick Emmanwori lays down challenge that drove success vs. Kenneth Walker III Related: Seahawks’ Mike Macdonald issues clear reminder to rest of NFL after Chiefs takedown

item.title: Mike Brown gets brutally honest as Knicks’ winless streak continues after loss to Magic
item.description: Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Mike Brown gets brutally honest as Knicks’ winless streak continues after loss to Magic appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Reality has come crashing down for the New York Knicks to begin the 2026-27 season. They may be the reigning NBA champion, but they surely aren’t playing like it. They have now lost all of their first three games to begin their title defense, with their most recent defeat coming at home to the Orlando Magic, 111-102. So far, championship hangover is proving to be a legitimate thing for the Knicks. They’ve been losing ground in the second half of games, and on Sunday, they allowed the Magic to outscore them by 13 points in the fourth quarter — with Orlando turning the tables on last season’s comeback kings. Suffice to say, these first few games of the new season have been quite the big slap to the Knicks’ face as a collective — with head coach Mike Brown even admitting that their team is just flat-out playing poorly at the moment. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “The biggest thing is to coach them and tell them the truth… If we’re trying, and trying the right way, sometimes you’ve got to fight through stuff like this to get yourself on track. Games like this will tell us like, our crap stinks. It does,” Brown said in his postgame presser, via SNY Knicks on X. "The biggest thing is to coach them and tell them the truth… If we're trying, and trying the right way, sometimes you've got to fight through stuff like this to get yourself on track. Games like this will tell us like, our crap stinks. It does." – Mike Brown pic.twitter.com/32sgBqXXqM — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 26, 2026 The most recent time that a defending champion went 0-3 to start the season came back in 2011 , when the Dallas Mavericks lost their first three contests of the season. The Mavs would finish the lockout-shortened season with a 36-30 record, and they would get swept in the first round of the playoffs by the upstart Oklahoma City Thunder. Dallas wouldn’t sniff title contention again until 2024. There seems to be general sense of lethargy that is plaguing the Knicks’ play as of late, and the fatigue from last season appears to be carrying over to this campaign. It will take some time for New York to get it together, but the slate for them isn’t about to get any easier as the 3-0 Detroit Pistons will come into town on Tuesday night. Related: Knicks HC Mike Brown gets 100% real about decision to cut player for Dalton Knecht Related: Knicks match troubling trend last seen in 2011 after loss to Magic

item.description: The first batch of College Football Playoff rankings will be released Tuesday, November 3rd, and we still have a weekend of games before we know what all the records are. But let’s get there faster with what the first top 25 will likely be on a night when the planet will be slightly preoccupied with other polls and voting results. Along with our projection of what each team’s record will be after this coming weekend, here’s our call on how the committee will rank its top 25. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images 25. New Mexico Projected Record: 7-1 Up Next: at San Jose State The committee will like the win over North Dakota State and respect the 14-6 loss at Oklahoma. At the very least, the Lobos will be on the fringe of the top 25 with a shot to be front-and-center as the Group of Six champion representative if everything goes right. 24. Florida Projected Record: 5-3 Up Next: Georgia (in Atlanta) This obviously changes if the Gators beat Georgia, but they should still sneak into the top 25 with a reasonably close loss, thanks to wins over Ole Miss and Texas on the road, and at home against Auburn. 23. Boise State Projected Record: 7-1 Up Next: Texas State One of the more interesting early calls for the committee, yeah, Boise State is 7-1 with the one loss to Oregon, but for a program that hasn’t won a game over a Power Four program since 2019, that only goes so far. Beating Memphis and Western Michigan, though, will matter. 22. Northwestern Projected Record: 6-2 Up Next: at Oregon Does Northwestern beat Oregon? It’s certainly not a definite loss like it appeared to be before the season, but for now, let’s sheepishly predict a close Duck win. The problem then becomes the lack of great wins – that includes Penn State. 21. Cincinnati Projected Record: 6-2 Up Next: Utah This ranking is all about the call of a Cincinnati win over Utah this weekend to go along with the win over Texas Tech last Saturday. The loss to West Virginia is all that drags this ranking down. Oct 24, 2026; Tucson, Arizona, USA; Arizona Wildcats quarterback Noah Fifita (1) during the first quarter against the Iowa State Cyclones at Casino Del Sol Stadium. The overtime loss to UCF will hurt in the first round of rankings, but it won’t be a big deal as long as the Cougars keep winning. 6. The win over LSU, though, is what gets UK this high. 5. Indiana Projected Record: 8-1 Up Next: Minnesota Being the only team to beat Northwestern isn’t just everything; it’s the only thing. The room will respect the win at Michigan and will sort of like the 20-17 win over Nebraska, but that’s about it unless the team gets respect for coming this close to beating Ohio State. (Again, the committee almost never gives enough credit for good, tough losses.) 4. UCLA Projected Record: 8-0 Up Next: Nevada In the first week of November, Power Four 8-0 don’t care where 8-0 came from. The 17-7 win over Wisconsin will get the most credit, and beating Oregon in Eugene matters. But this is all about that zero in the right-hand column. If it were that easy –

item.title: Deshaun Watson’s remarkable return puts NFL award in reach despite Patrick Mahomes threat
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Deshaun Watson has emerged as a candidate for NFL Comeback Player of the Year after leading the Cleveland Browns to a 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans. The quarterback threw for 308 yards and recorded his fifth fourth-quarter game-winning drive of the season, helping the Browns improve to 5-2. Watson’s resurgence comes after two Achilles surgeries forced him to miss the entire 2025 season, making his return to form all the more notable. Deshaun Watson enters Comeback Player of the Year conversation Longtime Browns insider Mary Kay Cabot believes Watson deserves consideration for the award, although she acknowledged that Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes remains the favourite. “Deshaun Watson has gone from not knowing if he could ever play in front of Browns fans again to becoming a legitimate candidate for NFL Comeback Player of the Year,” Cabot said. “Of course, the Chiefs’ Patrick Mahomes is clearly the frontrunner for that coveted postseason award, but Watson, after pulling off his fifth fourth-quarter game-winning drive of the season in Sunday’s 27-24 victory over the Titans, has to at least be in the conversation.” Mahomes entered the gameweek as a minus-175 favourite, according to DraftKings, with Watson among the other players in contention. Watson strengthened his case with his best passing performance since joining Cleveland. He completed 25 of 36 attempts against Tennessee, overcame an early interception and added a rushing touchdown. After his nine-yard scoring run gave the Browns a 24-17 lead, the Titans levelled the game with 58 seconds remaining. Watson responded with a 36-yard completion to Harold Fannin Jr., setting up Andre Szmyt’s winning 32-yard field goal. Head coach Todd Monken praised Watson’s ability to deliver under pressure, while also calling for greater consistency earlier in games. The award’s criteria could also work in Watson’s favour, with the Associated Press emphasising players overcoming injuries or other circumstances that forced them to miss time. However, Mahomes remains the leading contender, and Watson will need to maintain his form as Cleveland’s season continues. His performances over the coming weeks could determine whether his comeback becomes an award-winning story. item.title: Juventus ride production from midfield for victory over Lecce
item.description: LECCE, ITALY - OCTOBER 25: Weston McKennie of Juventus FC after scoring a goal to make it 0-1 during the Serie A match between US Lecce and Juventus at Stadio Via del Mare on October 25, 2026 in Lecce, Italy. (Photo by Ivan Romano/Getty Images) | Getty Images April 6, 2026. That was the last time that Juventus had gone into the half up 2-0 or better until Sunday’s matchup against Lecce. That April 6 match against Genoa saw Juve go 2-0 up on goals from Bremer and Weston McKennie and hold that advantage for the rest of the match. It took the Bianconeri a little longer at the Stadio Via del Mare, but it was finally McKennie in the 29th minute who nestled a lofted free kick from Douglas Luiz into the net to open the scoring. Luiz then struck himself four minutes shy of the break with a long-range strike that came off the hand of goalkeeper Wladimiro Falcone and then off the inside of the post. It was a day of firsts in the Juve midfield: McKennie’s first goal of the season, Luiz’s first goal and first assist in a Juventus shirt (it’s only been two years and a quarter or so), and the first time in Luiz’s career he’d ever had one of each. It wasn’t an explosive, dominant win that evoked visions of a team turning the corner — frankly, I don’t think we can expect that until the biggest players on the club’s titanic injury list finally return — and there were moments of the second half where that two-goal lead felt anything but secure. But after the demoralizing loss to Lazio last week and the infuriating draw against Rennes in midweek, a victory of any kind is a welcome, and Juve did hold that 2-0 victory to hopefully start a small run of momentum heading into what should be a winnable run of games. Luciano Spalletti came into the match under intense pressure, and dealing with an even longer injury list after losing two more players, Nico González and Zeki Çelik, on Thursday. They joined Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram, Francisco Conceição, Jeff Ekhator, and Kamil Grabara on the injured list. Spalletti replicated his 3-4-1-2 setup from Thursday’s game against Rennes, with two changes. Guglielmo Vicario started behind the three-man back line of Federico Gatti, Bremer, and Jhon Lucumí. Pierre Kalulu and Andrea Cambiaso took up the wing-back spots around the midfield pivot of Luiz and Teun Koopmeiners. McKennie took up station in the hole behind Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani. Lecce manager Eusebio Di Francesco won his 200th career game last week against Udinese. item.content:encoded: LECCE, ITALY - OCTOBER 25: Weston McKennie of Juventus FC after scoring a goal to make it 0-1 during the Serie A match between US Lecce and Juventus at Stadio Via del Mare on October 25, 2026 in Lecce, Italy. (Photo by Ivan Romano/Getty Images) | Getty Images April 6, 2026. That was the last time that Juventus had gone into the half up 2-0 or better until Sunday’s matchup against Lecce. That April 6 match against Genoa saw Juve go 2-0 up on goals from Bremer and Weston McKennie and hold that advantage for the rest of the match. It took the Bianconeri a little longer at the Stadio Via del Mare, but it was finally McKennie in the 29th minute who nestled a lofted free kick from Douglas Luiz into the net to open the scoring. Luiz then struck himself four minutes shy of the break with a long-range strike that came off the hand of goalkeeper Wladimiro Falcone and then off the inside of the post. It was a day of firsts in the Juve midfield: McKennie’s first goal of the season, Luiz’s first goal and first assist in a Juventus shirt (it’s only been two years and a quarter or so), and the first time in Luiz’s career he’d ever had one of each. It wasn’t an explosive, dominant win that evoked visions of a team turning the corner — frankly, I don’t think we can expect that until the biggest players on the club’s titanic injury list finally return — and there were moments of the second half where that two-goal lead felt anything but secure. But after the demoralizing loss to Lazio last week and the infuriating draw against Rennes in midweek, a victory of any kind is a welcome, and Juve did hold that 2-0 victory to hopefully start a small run of momentum heading into what should be a winnable run of games. Luciano Spalletti came into the match under intense pressure, and dealing with an even longer injury list after losing two more players, Nico González and Zeki Çelik, on Thursday. They joined Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram, Francisco Conceição, Jeff Ekhator, and Kamil Grabara on the injured list. Spalletti replicated his 3-4-1-2 setup from Thursday’s game against Rennes, with two changes. Guglielmo Vicario started behind the three-man back line of Federico Gatti, Bremer, and Jhon Lucumí. Pierre Kalulu and Andrea Cambiaso took up the wing-back spots around the midfield pivot of Luiz and Teun Koopmeiners. McKennie took up station in the hole behind Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani. Lecce manager Eusebio Di Francesco won his 200th career game last week against Udinese. He was missing midfield mainstay Lassana Coulibaly, Ivan Ilic, Santiago Perotti, and Medon Berisha, but set up his remaining charges in his usual 4-3-3. Falcone captained the team from between the sticks, covered by the defense of Danilo Veiga, Kialonda Gaspar, Tiago Gabriel, and Antonino Gallo. Youssef Maleh, Oumar Ngom, and Mohamed Kaba were the midfield trio, while Konan N’Dri, Willem Geubbels, and Amar Fatah formed the attacking trident. The game very nearly started with a disaster. Seconds after the opening whistle, Vicario let himself be closed down by N’Dri and was lucky to see the latter’s deflection of his pass fly wide of the post. He very nearly let it happen again on the ensuing goal kick before he was finally able to get the ball out of danger. The overall offense didn’t look all that much better than it has in the last few games. Individual players like McKennie would get the ball into good positions only for no one to be able to do anything with it — or the reverse, like when Kolo Muani made a good run into the middle of the box only for Cambiaso to miss him by several yards with the pass. Neither team managed a shot over the first 20 minutes, and Juve were closing in on half an hour without taking a shot as they lined up to take a free kick in the middle of the field about 40 yards from goal. Koopmeiners had been standing over it while referee Fabio Maresca dealt with any shenanigans in the box, and just as he blew his whistle Luiz stepped back and snapped a floated ball into the middle of the box. McKennie made a perfect run to it and beat Falcone, who got himself caught in no man’s land.on the slide, side-footing it past the keeper to pay dirt. Just a few minutes later, Kolo Muani might’ve doubled the lead, but Koopmeners’ headed cross bounced off his shin and behind the goal, then Bremer missed a quick header off a corner kick. But Juve sent the goal kick right back where it came from, and after a quick series of passes got the ball upfield, Gatti squared the ball off to Luiz, who hit a first-time shot from outside the box. Falcone dove and got a hand to it, but couldn’t push it far enough. It pinged off the inside of the post and nestled into the net to double the Juve lead. The visitors went into the half having controlled 66 percent of possession. That quickly changed as the second period began. Within five minutes Lecce had forced two saves out of Vicario — neither particularly tricky — and had forced another two last-ditch blocks to keep the keeper from having to make a play. They slowly forced Juve onto the defensive, while the Bianconeri had to fling the ball upfield to try to generate any offense on the counter. The pressure started to get to Juve as the half wore on, and some uncharacteristic mistakes began to creep into their attempts at breaking out. Lucumí overran his own dribble and gave the ball away deep, but Maleh fired his shot well wide. With about 20 minutes left Geubbles was put into a good position into the channel and really ought to have at least forced something out of Vicario, but fired over instead. Vicario himself misplaced a few passes to leave Lecce with a short field. Additional saves against Paco Esteban and N’Dri seemed to mark the end of the real push. In the last 10 minutes Lecce’s attack petered out and Juve finally regained some semblance of equilibrium. Jérémie Boga and Juan Cabal— yes, Juan Cabal played in this game of the season — each fired shots high in those last 10, the latter coming from relatively close range. The game’s final phases were dominated by the last-minute red card to Gaspar, who clearly crossed a line with Maresca while arguing over the award of a late corner kick, with the referee not even bothering to pull out a second yellow (Gaspar had been booked in the 76th minute) and simply went for a straight red instead. The final whistle came seconds later, and the Bianconeri were headed back to Turin with three important points.

item.title: Devdutt Padikkal left fuming after controversial umpiring decision ends his knock on 199 vs New Zealand A
item.description: Devdutt Padikkal left fuming after controversial umpiring decision ends his knock on 199 vs New Zealand A originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Devdutt Padikkal missed a double century by one run, scoring 199 during India A's first unofficial Test against New Zealand A. He was given out caught behind off Zak Gibson in an umpiring decision that left him furious. With no DRS available in unofficial Tests, Padikkal could not challenge the decision. Devdutt Padikkal misses double century by one run after controversial dismissal Devdutt Padikkal was unhappy after a controversial umpiring call that forced him out at 199 for India A against New Zealand A in Lincoln on Monday, October 26. The India A batter needed just one more run to score his maiden double century in the game when he was adjudged out caught behind off fast bowler Zak Gibson. His innings was crucial in helping India A overcome a tricky situation during the first unofficial Test match. Padikkal seemed upset about the umpiring call and showed his unhappiness before finally leaving the ground. Since there was no Decision Review System (DRS) in unofficial Test matches, he could not have any recourse to it. - 32(77) in first innings. - 199(248) in second innings. Two tough situations, Devdutt Padikkal has overcome the first test in New Zealand, great signs for Two match Test series 🤞 He has sealed the Number 3 spot in Indian Test Cricket. https://t.co/haqcP4illX — Johns. (@CricCrazyJohns) October 26, 2026 MORE: New Zealand A vs India A 1st unofficial Test: Scores, key highlights Padikkal furious after controversial decision ends his knock on 199 Padikkal was bowled a delivery by Gibson down the leg side. On 199, Padikkal tried to work it down the leg side but looked like he missed it, and the ball appeared to have brushed off his pads before reaching wicketkeeper Mitchell Hay. New Zealand A players appealed for a catch behind, and umpire Brad Wilson raised his finger. Padikkal immediately looked towards the umpire in disbelief, gesturing that the ball had gone far from his bat. He stayed on the ground for a while, looking disappointed at the umpiring before leaving the ground. It was evident that he was unhappy with the umpiring, given how close he was to achieving his goal. Padikkal scored 199 runs off 248 balls with 24 fours and 3 sixes. 🔴DEVDUTT PADIKKAL ANGRY OVER A CONTROVERSIAL UMPIRING DECISION! 🤯 - Padikkal was batting on 199 when the bowler delivered the ball wide. - Padikkal tried to play the delivery, but the umpire suddenly declared him out, apparently believing the ball had edged the bat. - Padikkal was left shocked by the decision. Note: There is no DRS in unofficial Test matches. ❌ https://t.co/WfZMaQfAXM — Sam (@cricsam02) October 26, 2026 MORE: India's 'bland, heartless' pitches slammed after IND-A collapses in NZ Test Padikkal's 199 rescues India A after early collapse India A got all out for 113 runs

item.title: From outranking the Fab Four to fight for his place: Rise, reign and the unraveling of Marnus Labuschagne
item.description: 'What the hell is that?' screamed Simon Katich from the commentary box as Marnus Labuschagne threw his wicket away in the second innings of the second Test against South Africa. Australia had been forced to follow on and were only beginning to recover when their number three handed the hosts another opening. Labuschagne had batted patiently to reach 39 before dancing down the track to off-spinner Simon Harmer and attempting to hit him over the long-on boundary. He failed to clear the ropes and holed out to Marco Jansen. The brain fade laid waste to the 92-run partnership between Labuschagne and Travis Head as the visitors were trying to hang on for a draw. Australia eventually lost the Test by an innings and 31 runs. For Labuschagne, it was another failure to build on after getting the start. In four innings on the South Africa tour, in the country where he was born, the Australian batter has been dismissed in the thirties three times. For a batter who once seemed to have found a permanent home among the world's best, the struggle to convert starts into big scores has become a recurring problem of late. When Marnus ruled the world and outranked Fab Four After an unremarkable start to his career, he earned a place in Australia's squad for the 2019 Ashes in England. He was not among the biggest names in a team packed with established players, but the series would change his place in Australian cricket. At Lord's, Steve Smith was struck on the neck by a Jofra Archer bouncer and had to leave the field. Labuschagne came in as Test cricket's first concussion substitute, taking the place of a batter who was himself in the middle of a remarkable comeback. Under overcast skies, with England pressing for a win on the fifth day, Labuschagne scored 59 and helped Australia escape defeat. That innings proved to be a turning point. Over the following summer, Labuschagne went from a promising batter to one of the most consistent run-scorers in Test cricket. Against Pakistan, he scored 347 runs at an average of 173.50. He followed that with 549 runs at 91.50 against New Zealand, establishing himself as a key figure in Australia's Test batting line-up. His form continued in 2021, despite the challenges of playing through Covid restrictions. By the Boxing Day Test that year, Labuschagne had climbed to the top of the ICC Test batting rankings, ahead of Steve Smith, Joe Root, Virat Kohli and Kane Williamson — the four players Martin Crowe had famously grouped as the 'Fab Four'. A long way down from the top Between 2019 and 2022, Labuschagne scored 2,990 runs in 50 innings at an average of 62.3. He hit 10 centuries and 13 fifties during that period. Since 2023, however, his returns have declined disastrously. In 66 innings between 2023 and 2026 so far, he has averaged 29.7, scoring 12 fifties and just one century. item.content:encoded: 'What the hell is that?' screamed Simon Katich from the commentary box as Marnus Labuschagne threw his wicket away in the second innings of the second Test against South Africa. Australia had been forced to follow on and were only beginning to recover when their number three handed the hosts another opening. Labuschagne had batted patiently to reach 39 before dancing down the track to off-spinner Simon Harmer and attempting to hit him over the long-on boundary. He failed to clear the ropes and holed out to Marco Jansen. The brain fade laid waste to the 92-run partnership between Labuschagne and Travis Head as the visitors were trying to hang on for a draw. Australia eventually lost the Test by an innings and 31 runs. For Labuschagne, it was another failure to build on after getting the start. In four innings on the South Africa tour, in the country where he was born, the Australian batter has been dismissed in the thirties three times. For a batter who once seemed to have found a permanent home among the world's best, the struggle to convert starts into big scores has become a recurring problem of late. When Marnus ruled the world and outranked Fab Four After an unremarkable start to his career, he earned a place in Australia's squad for the 2019 Ashes in England. He was not among the biggest names in a team packed with established players, but the series would change his place in Australian cricket. At Lord's, Steve Smith was struck on the neck by a Jofra Archer bouncer and had to leave the field. Labuschagne came in as Test cricket's first concussion substitute, taking the place of a batter who was himself in the middle of a remarkable comeback. Under overcast skies, with England pressing for a win on the fifth day, Labuschagne scored 59 and helped Australia escape defeat. That innings proved to be a turning point. Over the following summer, Labuschagne went from a promising batter to one of the most consistent run-scorers in Test cricket. Against Pakistan, he scored 347 runs at an average of 173.50. He followed that with 549 runs at 91.50 against New Zealand, establishing himself as a key figure in Australia's Test batting line-up. His form continued in 2021, despite the challenges of playing through Covid restrictions. By the Boxing Day Test that year, Labuschagne had climbed to the top of the ICC Test batting rankings, ahead of Steve Smith, Joe Root, Virat Kohli and Kane Williamson — the four players Martin Crowe had famously grouped as the 'Fab Four'. A long way down from the top Between 2019 and 2022, Labuschagne scored 2,990 runs in 50 innings at an average of 62.3. He hit 10 centuries and 13 fifties during that period. Since 2023, however, his returns have declined disastrously. In 66 innings between 2023 and 2026 so far, he has averaged 29.7, scoring 12 fifties and just one century. That hundred came in Manchester during the 2023 Ashes. The decline is particularly clear against pace bowling, once an area in which Labuschagne excelled. In 2020 and 2021, he averaged 76 and 74 against fast and medium-fast bowlers, respectively. From 2019 to 2022, his overall average against fast and medium-fast bowlers stood at 59.2. Since 2023, that number has dropped to just 28. In 2025, it fell to 18. From Australia's safety net to its loose thread In Test cricket, the number three position carries a particular mythologised lineage. It has been occupied by players such as Don Bradman and Ricky Ponting for Australia. Kumar Sangakkara played at first drop for Sri Lanka, Hashim Amla played that role for South Africa, and Rahul Dravid made that spot synonymous with himself for India. During his peak years, Labuschagne appeared to be Australia's long-term answer to the position. Among batters who played at least 15 innings at number three between 2019 and 2023, excluding players from Zimbabwe, Ireland and Afghanistan, Labuschagne averaged 65.85. Only Williamson, with an average of 67.16, was ahead of him. Since 2023, however, Labuschagne's average at number three has fallen to 31.72. Among the same group of batters who played at least 15 innings at the position between 2019 and 2023, he now has the lowest average. A number three, or any batter, can not make a hundred every time he walks out. There will be difficult conditions, good bowling and innings in which survival is the primary task. But the position demands a degree of reliability because the consequences of failure are often felt by the middle order. That is where Labuschagne's recent returns become particularly troubling. He is not consistently falling at the first hurdle. He is surviving long enough to create the expectation of a big innings, then failing to meet it. What is Labuschagne doing wrong? Labuschagne turned 32 in June, an age at which a Test batter would ordinarily expect to combine experience with technical and tactical maturity. He has played enough cricket to recognise different bowling plans and has spent years facing the world's best attacks. Yet his recent performances suggest that experience alone has not helped him find a solution. In the two Tests of the South Africa series, he has scored 37, 37, 14 and 39. Across his last eight innings, he has crossed 30 on five occasions but has repeatedly failed to go much further. Former Australia captain Greg Chappell believes Labuschagne's struggles may be part of a wider pattern that affects elite players after years at the top. In an article published in June 2025, Chappell described it as 'Elite Performance Decline Syndrome'. Speaking to Fox Sports last month, Chappell suggested that Labuschagne could be experiencing this phase of his career, with a decline in his average and influence accompanied by a loss of mental resilience. “Marnus is at the stage of his career that we all get to,” Chappell told Fox Sport last month. “What did I call it? I wrote an article: Elite Performance Decline Syndrome. You’ve got a finite number of innings in you and you sort of run out." That is one explanation, but there are also technical questions. Some observers believe Labuschagne is getting too front-on with his chest when defending, leaving him vulnerable to edges that carry to the slips. That was evident in the first innings of the second Test, when he edged Anrich Nortje to Simon Harmer. Australia captain Pat Cummins, however, has pointed towards decision-making rather than a fundamental flaw in technique. Labuschagne's attempt to hit Harmer over the boundary in the second innings was a case in point. Australia were batting to save the match, and the conditions, including a strong wind, offered little reason to take such a risk. “It’s certainly not a technique error. It’s ... maybe a couple of decision-making, some decisions (when) maybe the game demanded something a little bit different,” Cummins said. How much faith can a reputation buy? Labuschagne has been afforded more chances than most, but Australian cricket has a history of punishing batters whose judgement deserts them against South Africa. Damien Martyn's attempted airborne cover drive off Allan Donald in 1994 contributed to a six-year absence from the Test team. Brad Hodge, meanwhile, was dismissed by Andre Nel at the SCG in 2006 and subsequently lost his place. Labuschagne's situation is not identical to either case, but could he become the Proteas' third victim? Cummins has acknowledged that Labuschagne is doing the difficult part by reaching the 30s against an attack that has been making life uncomfortable for Australia's batters. But he has also made clear that those starts are not enough. “The balls are normally doing a fair bit. You got fresh bowlers, and he’s actually doing the hard bit (by) getting to 30s. I think he’s got to find a way to turn those into bigger scores (because) 30s aren’t going to win you too many matches," Cummins said after the second Test. item.title: LAFC's furious El Tráfico comeback sparks confidence boost ahead of playoffs
item.description: LAFC's furious El Tráfico comeback sparks confidence boost ahead of playoffs By Alex Ruiz LOS ANGELES – Are you not entertained!?! A wild 2-2 draw between the LA Galaxy and LAFC on Sunday Night Soccer presented by Continental Tire added another gem to the collection of classic El Tráfico matches. A brace from Ghanaian international forward Joseph Paintsil gave the Galaxy an early buffer and quieted the BMO Stadium crowd. But LAFC’s superstars wouldn’t let their team go down without a fight. Confidence boost Denis Bouanga scored his 18th goal of the season with his 53rd-minute strike. Then, Leo Walta netted the game-tying goal 10 minutes later with the help of Son Heung-Min , whose 15 assists this season are tied for first in MLS with Inter Miami ’s Lionel Messi and FC Cincinnati ’s Evander . With this result, LAFC secured a spot in the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs in front of its home fans. “We are very happy, the club, the players, all of us. We fight for that, and I think we have to be happy because it's not easy for anyone,” Interim head coach Xavi Tamarit said. “I want to say that I am very proud about the team with the team, how we overcame a really difficult situation,” he added. “I think we're a team that we're showing that we're willing to fight even in tough times,” said captain and defender Aaron Long. “I think tonight was a was a you know not the result that we wanted in terms of a tie, but some ties feel better than others”. Bouanga balls out With his goal on the night, Bouanga has scored in eight straight regular-season matches against the Galaxy. Postgame, the Gabon winger made clear his intentions each time he lines up against LAFC's cross-town rivals. "I want to kill this team, and I don't know. I score so many goals against them and I love it,” Bouanga said to reporters. Even with the individual praise on the night, he’s focused on what LAFC can do in the postseason. “We can do something in the playoffs for sure. Some teams don't want to play against us,” said Bouanga. Following Sunday's heart-pounding El Tráfico, only two regular-season games remain for LAFC. Next up for the Black & Gold? A home match against Minnesota United next Sunday (8:30 pm | Apple TV ). WATCH: El Tráfico delivers! LAFC, LA Galaxy battle to wild draw

Postgame, the Gabon winger made clear his intentions each time he lines up against LAFC's cross-town rivals. "I want to kill this team, and I don't know. I score so many goals against them and I love it,” Bouanga said to reporters. Even with the individual praise on the night, he’s focused on what LAFC can do in the postseason. “We can do something in the playoffs for sure. Some teams don't want to play against us,” said Bouanga. Following Sunday's heart-pounding El Tráfico, only two regular-season games remain for LAFC. Next up for the Black & Gold? A home match against Minnesota United next Sunday (8:30 pm | Apple TV ). WATCH: El Tráfico delivers! LAFC, LA Galaxy battle to wild draw

item.title: Broncos’ Sean Payton Hints At A Massive Change At RB Position
item.description: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos reacts after defeating the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) Getty Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman wasted little time reminding the team what they’ve been missing amid his four-game absence. The fourth-round selection finished with nine attempts for 54 yards and caught both of his targets for 15 yards. He helped Denver secure an impressive 30-16 victory on the road and effectively made head coach Sean Payton another reason to rethink the team’s backfield rotation. When speaking to reporters after the contest, Payton said, “Got to get him more touches. Definitely.” This is Coleman’s second promising performance of the season, as he also carried the ball ten times for 39 yards and a rushing score in their Week 2 win over Jacksonville. He also added three catches for 19 yards in that gamr. Jonah Coleman Might’ve Taken Lead Back Duties For Broncos The Broncos have been desperately searching for consistency and explosiveness on the ground. Entering today’s contest, J.K. Dobbins had a mere 270 yards off 81 carries (3.4 yards-per-attempt). He started hot with three attempts for 15 yards on the first drive today, but only had three carries for eight yards the rest of the way. Meanwhile, RJ Harvey has established himself as a key weapon in the passing game, but he has only 87 yards off 24 attempts (3.6 yards-per-attempt). While both Harvey and Dobbins reached the end zone today, it was clear which back had the most impressive performance (surprisingly, the only one who failed to score a touchdown). Many were excited about Coleman during training camp, as he received rave reviews throughout August. Denver’s crowded backfield was really the only factor limiting his potential ceiling. However, he has more than enough talent to ascend the loaded depth chart. The fact that Payton clearly took note of the performance is a great indication of his trajectory. He’ll be a staple of their rushing attack going forward, even if Dobbins and Harvey will also remain involved. Jonah Coleman’s Emergence Throws Cold Water On Previous Trade Speculation Coleman’s emergence creates an interesting situation for the Broncos’ backfield. Conversely, it also extinguishes any potential trades that the team could make to bolster their running back room. Just last week, NFL analyst Kay Adams urged Sean Payton and Co. to trade for Colts Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor. “Sean [Payton], listen to me. Go get JT [Jonathan Taylor].” Adams said. “If they go get JT, they’re winning the Super Bowl. I’m saying it right now.” As it stands right now, that seems like a costly measure that is no longer necessary. DenSports 104.3 ‘s Andrew Mason also doesn’t believe they’ll go that route. “Jonah Coleman looks GOOD today,” Mason wrote on X. “Get him some more reps the next two games and the Broncos might have their answer wi

item.title: ‘Hanging by a thread’: Sky provide bleak update on Carrick’s future as INEOS line up two successors
item.description: ‘Hanging by a thread’: Sky provide bleak update on Carrick’s future as INEOS line up two successors Manchester United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday afternoon will seemingly mark the final game in Michael Carrick’s short-lived tenure. Less than a year after he was appointed to steady the ship in the aftermath of Ruben Amorim’s sacking, the former Red is facing the same fate himself. Michael Carrick: The state of play (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Sky Sports News shared an update last night claiming Carrick’s future as United manager was ‘hanging by a thread’. It’s said that INEOS had already decided they wanted to part ways with him before the defeat to the Cherries, but the side’s dismal display set it in stone. At full-time, Carrick was serenaded by the Old Trafford faithful with his chant while he made his way around the stadium applauding supporters, who swiftly switched to loud booing when the manager departed down the tunnel and the players made their way off the pitch. The result left United 16th-placed in the Premier League table after eight matches, while they also sit 20th in the Champions League rankings, having lost their last two group-phase games. United chiefs shortlist two potential replacements (Photo by Alex Davidson/Getty Images) In regard to who is set to take over, Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are now favourites. Unai Emery has been considered, but he is fully committed to staying at Aston Villa. Howe and Nagelsmann are both free agents, making INEOS’ life easier when it comes to negotiations. When directly asked whether he was expecting to be relieved of his duties by reporters post-match, Carrick said: “I totally understand the situation. I’m not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. I’m carrying on as normal and, you know, I love this place. “I always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club. Whatever decision is made on anything, really. Leave a Reply Cancel reply Your email address will not be published. item.title: United can make a huge statement by hiring Didier Deschamps who is a free agent
item.description: United can make a huge statement by hiring Didier Deschamps who is a free agent The chants at Old Trafford on Sunday suggested that fans feel the end is near, as they showcased their admiration for Michael Carrick and expressed their rage at the Glazers and INEOS. The 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth once again highlighted that Carrick, who cut a dejected figure at the full-time whistle, has lost control of the ship, and the arrival of a new man at the helm is now a matter of when, rather than if. What Man United are lacking Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have so far shown they are incapable of making courageous decisions for England’s biggest club, with both playing it safe instead of making ambitious and proactive moves. These are the same men who were trying to replace Erik ten Hag in 2024 before changing their minds after the Dutchman won the FA Cup. To no one’s surprise, the result of one match did not fix the frailties of Ten Hag’s tactics, and he got the axe a few weeks later, disrupting another season. Ruben Amorim oversaw the worst league finish in over 50 years, lost the Europa League final to Tottenham Hotspur, and offered to walk away with nothing, and yet, the pair sat down with folded hands, allowing another misfit to lead the Red Devils into a new campaign. Amorim had to take aim at Wilcox for the latter to finally pull the trigger at the turn of this year. The former Manchester City figures struck gold with Carrick, a club legend, who initially got players on his side and churned out excellent results, but did not have the pedigree to force INEOS out of their comfort zone in the summer and address glaring issues in the squad. Once again, the pair seemed to enjoy a summer of inaction, ultimately paving the way for a car crash of a season. As such, we are back to talking about new managerial candidates. It has been widely suggested that Wilcox *drum roll* prefers to make a Premier League-proven appointment, like most of his signings. As fans, it is futile to expect Sir Jim Ratcliffe to show Berrada and Wilcox the exit door, so all we can hope for is that the duo learn from their past mistakes and make a real change in the dugout by bringing in a manager with enough pedigree to not only make overpaid United stars do their talking on the pitch but also to challenge the hierarchy to match his standards. Among the potential options who are without a club, Antonio Conte, who has won trophies in Italy and England, has emerged as a popular name, but the Italian tactician could be too volatile for INEOS’s taste. The 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth once again highlighted that Carrick, who cut a dejected figure at the full-time whistle, has lost control of the ship, and the arrival of a new man at the helm is now a matter of when, rather than if. What Man United are lacking Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have so far shown they are incapable of making courageous decisions for England’s biggest club, with both playing it safe instead of making ambitious and proactive moves. These are the same men who were trying to replace Erik ten Hag in 2024 before changing their minds after the Dutchman won the FA Cup. To no one’s surprise, the result of one match did not fix the frailties of Ten Hag’s tactics, and he got the axe a few weeks later, disrupting another season. Ruben Amorim oversaw the worst league finish in over 50 years, lost the Europa League final to Tottenham Hotspur, and offered to walk away with nothing, and yet, the pair sat down with folded hands, allowing another misfit to lead the Red Devils into a new campaign. Amorim had to take aim at Wilcox for the latter to finally pull the trigger at the turn of this year. The former Manchester City figures struck gold with Carrick, a club legend, who initially got players on his side and churned out excellent results, but did not have the pedigree to force INEOS out of their comfort zone in the summer and address glaring issues in the squad. Once again, the pair seemed to enjoy a summer of inaction, ultimately paving the way for a car crash of a season. As such, we are back to talking about new managerial candidates. It has been widely suggested that Wilcox *drum roll* prefers to make a Premier League-proven appointment, like most of his signings. As fans, it is futile to expect Sir Jim Ratcliffe to show Berrada and Wilcox the exit door, so all we can hope for is that the duo learn from their past mistakes and make a real change in the dugout by bringing in a manager with enough pedigree to not only make overpaid United stars do their talking on the pitch but also to challenge the hierarchy to match his standards. Among the potential options who are without a club, Antonio Conte, who has won trophies in Italy and England, has emerged as a popular name, but the Italian tactician could be too volatile for INEOS’s taste. Didier Deschamps is an ideal manager to pick up the fallen giant Accordingly, we believe United should bring in Didier Deschamps to turn around their fortunes. The Frenchman is available after leaving his 14-year role as France’s manager following the summer’s World Cup. Les Bleus, akin to United, were a sleeping giant when he took over in 2012. The broken side went on strike under Raymond Domenech during the 2010 World Cup before enduring an underwhelming spell under Laurent Blanc. Deschamps , who captained France to the World Cup in 1998 as a midfielder, steadily put the house in order and led them to the same trophy as a manager in 2018. The 58-year-old also has extensive experience when it comes to managing at club level, having been on the touchline for AS Monaco, Juventus, and Marseille. Monaco reached the Champions League final and Marseille won their first league title in 18 years under his tutelage. Known for his pragmatic approach, based around an organised defence and free-flowing attack, Deschamps has both the tactical nous and man-management skills to deal with the challenges a United manager faces. The French legend is a manager with an impeccable résumé whom INEOS would be fortunate to get their hands on.

item.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba makes Super Bowl era history as Seahawks beat Chiefs
item.description: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Jaxon Smith-Njigba makes Super Bowl era history as Seahawks beat Chiefs appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Put Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the NFL in the late 1960s. How many receiving yards would he tally in a season? 2,000? 4,000? 58,000? Smith-Njigba and the Seahawks handed the Kansas City Chiefs their first loss , rolling to a dominant victory, 20-3, at Lumen Field on Sunday. Smith-Njigba had nine receptions for 150 yards and one touchdown. He also had two carries for 13 yards. The 24-year-old star reminded everyone why he is the reigning Offensive Player of the Year, as he made history against the Chiefs. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the first player in the Super Bowl Era (since 1966) with at least 850 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns in his team’s first seven games of the season,” said ESPN Insights. Last season, he led the league with a career-high 1,793 receiving yards. He also recorded a career-high 10 touchdowns. Smith-Njigba is on track to surpass those numbers, or even threaten his teammate Cooper Kupp’s spot for the second-most receiving yards in a season. Kupp tallied 1,947 receiving yards with the Los Angeles Rams in 2021. NFL legend Calvin Johnson owns the all-time record with 1,964 receiving yards with the Detroit Lions in 2012. The Seahawks snapped a two-game skid and improved to 4-3, including 3-1 at home. The Chiefs fell to 5-1. Sam Darnold went 20-of-28 for 257 yards and one touchdown. Emanuel Wilson had 24 carries for 100 yards and a score. The defense also went to work, limiting the Chiefs to their lowest output since Week 18 in 2024. The Seahawks held Kenneth Walker III to just 36 yards on 14 carries in his first game against Seattle since signing with Kansas City in the offseason. Patrick Mahomes went 19-of-33 yards for 1645 yards and one interception. The Seahawks will host the Chicago Bears in Week 8. Related: Seahawks’ Nick Emmanwori lays down challenge that drove success vs. Kenneth Walker III Related: Seahawks’ Mike Macdonald issues clear reminder to rest of NFL after Chiefs takedown

item.title: NFL Gets Backlash for Critical Browns Blown Call
item.description: Harold Fannin Jr. #44 of the Cleveland Browns Getty It was another magical ending for the Cleveland Browns on the road in Tennessee on Sunday in Week 7, as the team locked up a 27-24 win on a field goal knocked through by Andre Szmyt with no time remaining on the clock. The kick came after a huge 36-yard catch-and-run from tight end Harold Fannin, who caught the pass from Deshaun Watson at about the 50-yard line with 25 seconds to play in a tie game, turned and rumbled another 30 yards down to the Titans‘ 19. That put Szmyt in position for the win. So the fairytale season moves ahead, with the Browns now 5-2 and in first place as they face a monster game against the 5-2 Steelers on the road next Sunday. The Browns beat the Steelers at home in Week 4, and a win in Pittsburgh would be like two wins for Cleveland, because it would seal the tiebreaker. Browns Clearly Guilty of False Start Not everyone was taken by the thrill of the Browns’ final drive, though. In fact, many poked a giant hole in it: right tackle Dawand Jones, in for Tytus Howard, clearly was guilty of a false start before the snap, moving out of his set and stepping back in pass protection a full beat before the ball was snapped. “I’ll have to look at the tape,” Titans coach Robert Saleh said after the game. “It looked like from live, I think they did (false start), yeah.” The ‘ TruthSeeker ” betting account, with 130,000 followers, wrote, “THE NFL IS 100% RIGGED. This was clearly a false start by the #Browns .” THE NFL IS 100% RIGGED. This was clearly a false start by the #Browns pic.twitter.com/ARkvGgVhx5 — Truth Seeker (@_TruthZone_) October 25, 2026 ‘Titans Were Robbed’ There was not much sentiment in favor of the Browns on that one, other than to point out that other calls against the Titans were missed, too. As @Matt_StCharles wrote, “Blown away by the amount of people acknowledging the false start but saying it didn’t impact the play. IF A FALSE START IS CALLED, THERE IS NO PLAY.” Ari Meirov of The 32nd Team noted, “I have no idea how there isn’t a false start on Cleveland here on the play that got them in FG range. I mean, c’mon.” Mike Florio o f Pro Football Talk, added , “It was very early. Noticeably earlier than the move perfected in recent years by Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson , who routinely utilized the technique of going at the perfect moment to give him a jump on blocking the pass rusher without having the plug on the play pulled by a false-start penalty. Jones didn’t just leave early. And he didn’t use the far more common single early step with his right foot. He jumped back , like he’d just seen a rattlesnake.” And from the Titans’ London fan site : “Seriously, how does every official with eyes miss this false start by the Browns RT on one of the biggest plays of the game? Our @Titans were robbed here.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post NFL Gets Backlash for Critical Browns Blown Call appeared first on HEAVY .
