item.title: Bucks Reportedly Turned Down Trade Offer From Nuggets Before Waiving Kevin Porter Jr.
item.description: Before the Milwaukee Bucks moved on from guard Kevin Porter Jr. , who had been with the Bucks for two seasons before being waived this past offseason, they had an option ahead of them to try and turn Porter Jr. into a productive trade package. The Bucks waived Porter Jr. after a fairly productive 2025-26 season where he averaged 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds and 7.4 assists per game after new acquisitions over the offseason essentially forced Porter Jr. out of what was suddenly a crowded guard room in Milwaukee, but before that, the Bucks could have capitalized on his value. Per a report from Marc Stein, the Bucks were presented with a trade offer for Porter Jr. from the Denver Nuggets, but the finances involved led the Bucks to walk away. Milwaukee Bucks guard Kevin Porter Jr. (7) drives on Charlotte Hornets guard Michael Ajayi (10) during the fourth quarter at Spectrum Center. Scott Kinser-Imagn Images “The Stein Line has learned that the Nuggets showed a willingness to package two future second-rounders and a second-round pick swap along with Zeke Nnaji's very available contract in a bid to bring Kevin Porter Jr. to the Rocky Mountains," Stein wrote . "Yet I'm told that the Bucks ultimately walked away... because they could not stomach the idea of swallowing Nnaji's $7.5 million salary for the 2027-28 season.” Avoiding Expensive Contracts Nnaji does have a very expensive contract considering how little production he has to show for it. Nnaji played 52 games last season in Denver, starting four, where he averaged just 3.7 points and 2.6 rebounds per game. Milwaukee Bucks guard Kevin Porter Jr. (7) shoots against the Charlotte Hornets during the fourth quarter at Spectrum Center. Scott Kinser-Imagn Images Pairing those numbers with the salary attached to him has made him an expensive issue for the Nuggets to deal with and an issue that the Bucks apparently wanted no part of. Prioritizing financial flexibility over simply filling roster space with Nnaji, who would have just as small of a role in Milwaukee playing behind big men like Myles Turner and Kel'el Ware that he's so far had in Denver, is a thrifty move on Milwaukee's part as the team tries to build for the future. Milwaukee Bucks guard/forward Kevin Porter Jr. (7) shoots against Cleveland Cavaliers guard James Harden (1) in the second half at Fiserv Forum. Michael McLoone-Imagn Images It still begs the question of why Porter Jr. didn't warrant more attention on the trade market if the Bucks didn't have any future plans for him, but the package that Denver presented would have been a step back for what the Bucks are trying to build. A New Philosophy in Milwaukee Maintaining flexibility is the right move for the Bucks to make for the foreseeable future as they try to further accumulate assets to future support the team's rebuild, and a crucial part of that process is for the Bucks to be discerning in the way that they accumulate those assets. item.content:encoded: Before the Milwaukee Bucks moved on from guard Kevin Porter Jr. , who had been with the Bucks for two seasons before being waived this past offseason, they had an option ahead of them to try and turn Porter Jr. into a productive trade package. The Bucks waived Porter Jr. after a fairly productive 2025-26 season where he averaged 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds and 7.4 assists per game after new acquisitions over the offseason essentially forced Porter Jr. out of what was suddenly a crowded guard room in Milwaukee, but before that, the Bucks could have capitalized on his value. Per a report from Marc Stein, the Bucks were presented with a trade offer for Porter Jr. from the Denver Nuggets, but the finances involved led the Bucks to walk away. Milwaukee Bucks guard Kevin Porter Jr. (7) drives on Charlotte Hornets guard Michael Ajayi (10) during the fourth quarter at Spectrum Center. Scott Kinser-Imagn Images “The Stein Line has learned that the Nuggets showed a willingness to package two future second-rounders and a second-round pick swap along with Zeke Nnaji's very available contract in a bid to bring Kevin Porter Jr. to the Rocky Mountains," Stein wrote . "Yet I'm told that the Bucks ultimately walked away... because they could not stomach the idea of swallowing Nnaji's $7.5 million salary for the 2027-28 season.” Avoiding Expensive Contracts Nnaji does have a very expensive contract considering how little production he has to show for it. Nnaji played 52 games last season in Denver, starting four, where he averaged just 3.7 points and 2.6 rebounds per game. Milwaukee Bucks guard Kevin Porter Jr. (7) shoots against the Charlotte Hornets during the fourth quarter at Spectrum Center. Scott Kinser-Imagn Images Pairing those numbers with the salary attached to him has made him an expensive issue for the Nuggets to deal with and an issue that the Bucks apparently wanted no part of. Prioritizing financial flexibility over simply filling roster space with Nnaji, who would have just as small of a role in Milwaukee playing behind big men like Myles Turner and Kel'el Ware that he's so far had in Denver, is a thrifty move on Milwaukee's part as the team tries to build for the future. Milwaukee Bucks guard/forward Kevin Porter Jr. (7) shoots against Cleveland Cavaliers guard James Harden (1) in the second half at Fiserv Forum. Michael McLoone-Imagn Images It still begs the question of why Porter Jr. didn't warrant more attention on the trade market if the Bucks didn't have any future plans for him, but the package that Denver presented would have been a step back for what the Bucks are trying to build. A New Philosophy in Milwaukee Maintaining flexibility is the right move for the Bucks to make for the foreseeable future as they try to further accumulate assets to future support the team's rebuild, and a crucial part of that process is for the Bucks to be discerning in the way that they accumulate those assets. Milwaukee Bucks guard Kevin Porter Jr. (7) drives on Atlanta Hawks forward Onyeka Okongwu (17) in the second quarter at State Farm Arena. Brett Davis-Imagn Images The package they could have received from the Nuggets clearly wasn't the way they wanted to move forward with Porter Jr. and considering that they already have players like forward Kyle Kuzma who is a large contract without producing much value for the team. Nnaji would have been a repeat of that kind of move for the Bucks, a methodology that the team is decidedly trying to move away from.

item.title: Fans Welcome Quinn Hughes Back To Vancouver With Boos, Canucks Fall 4-2 To The Wild
item.description: The Vancouver Canucks winless streak hit 10 as they fell 4-2 to the Minnesota Wild on Sunday night. Max Sasson scored on a breakaway, while Brock Boeser also found the back of the net in the loss. As for goaltending, Leevi Meriläinen had another strong night, stopping 30 of the 34 shots he faced. The main focus of Sunday's game was the return of Quinn Hughes . The former Canucks captain was once again dynamic as he scored, picked up an assist and led all players with 26:10 of ice time. Hughes also hit a milestone Sunday as he became the second-fastest American defenceman to record 500 regular-season points. Fans made their feelings known about Hughes from the opening puck drop. There were plenty of boos and chants from the Rogers Arena faithful all night. That being said, there were some cheers during the video tribute, but they were instantly met with boos as soon as play resumed. As for the game, it was once again a mess defensively. Vancouver struggled to get the puck out of their own zone, and could not control play in the neutral zone. Post-game, Luke Schenn and Manny Malhotra were asked about the defensive zone issues, with each giving their take on the defensive zone issues. "A lot of the time when you're hemmed in your own zone for a bit, it feels like you're just trying to survive," said Schenn. "Then you get it to the neutral zone, and you're just trying to chip it in and get a line change. So that probably could have something to do with it. I mean, obviously, we don't create a ton. So that probably starts in the D-zone, neutral zone. I mean, it's all connected. So tough to pinpoint." "It's a number of things," said Malhotra. "Lack of execution through the neutral zone. It's a lack of support through the neutral zone, which means we just stop skating. There's a lot of watching going on, especially in the second period. And when you watch in this league, pucks tend to come back into your zone." Lack of shots was also a theme yet again for the Canucks. After posting 10 in the first, Vancouver managed just seven over the final 40 minutes. Post-game, a visibly frustrated Malhotra gave his thoughts on his team's play in the offensive zone. "It's related to that lack of consistency in our effort," said Malhotra. "When we were direct in the first period, and we were applying pressure in the O-zone. Obviously, you create looks. You're able to get, number one, you're able to get pucks back to be able to shoot the puck. But again, when you come off of those things, and you're not applying the same pressure, you just don't get the same looks." While the wins and losses may not matter this season, effort does. Sunday was yet another game where Malhotra was unhappy with the effort level of his group, which is very telling 13 games into the season. Even though the campaign is only a month old, some very concerning trends are emerging from this team, and they were on full display in Sunday's loss. item.title: ‘Shout out to Ja’Marr Chase’ – JD Vance reacts to Cincinnati Bengals win over Baltimore Ravens
item.description: Credit: Roy Rochlin/Tim Warner via Getty Images Vice President JD Vance was happy to see his Cincinnati Bengals pick up a 35-13 win over the Baltimore Ravens in a huge divisional win. Vance visited the Bengals during practice for the Ravens matchup last week, drawing a lot of attention for his interactions with the players and how team QB Joe Burrow reacted to his attendance at practice. One of the few positive interactions from Vance’s visit to practice came from star WR Ja’Marr Chase, who spoke to the Vice President and made a comment about his six-year-old son’s gloves, something that Vance remembered even after the win. JD Vance’s reaction to Bengals win and shout-out for Ja’Marr Chase Vance took to X to share his thoughts on the Bengals win, giving a shoutout to star WR Chase as well. “Huge win for Cincinnati. Proud of the entire team, but a special shout-out to Ja’Marr Chase, an amazing talent, who made my little six-year-old’s year by noticing his football gloves. It’s early, but I think the Bengals are going to make a run. Who Dey!” This was an incredible win for the Bengals, who fell to a 13-0 deficit at halftime before scoring 35 unanswered points in the second half to pick up a comprehensive win. Chase finished with five receptions on seven targets for 62 yards and 1 touchdown, playing an efficient role in a signature win for the Bengals. While Chase has not been a high-volume receiver through the first few weeks of the season, his efficiency and ability to scale into bigger production are a very good sign for the Bengals’ offence. During Vance’s visit to Bengals practice on October 22, Chase spoke to the VP’s six-year-old son Vivek and complimented his football gloves, a moment that clearly left an indelible impression on Vance and his son. item.title: 49ers QB Brock Purdy Drops Honest Quote After Loss to Falcons
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 25: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers looks on after the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. The Falcons defeated the 49ers 29-20. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers fell 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, suffering their first loss of the NFL season after a 6-0 start. San Francisco’s offense turned the ball over four times, including two costly interceptions thrown by quarterback Brock Purdy and fumbles by running back Kaelon Black and tight end George Kittle. Purdy Drops Honest Quote After Loss After the loss, Purdy spoke about the offensive miscues that set the 49ers back, despite the team moving the ball and racking up yardage throughout the game. “We had the momentum, we were moving the ball well, I feel like we were running the ball really well offensively and then all of the sudden its like a couple plays make you feel like dang we’re not doing our job,” Purdy said. “Obviously the most important thing is protecting the football. That’s really the number one thing in our organization as an offense… and so when you do have those kind of costly mistakes it does make you feel like alright we’re not doing anything, we’re not putting up points like we need too… it starts with me at quarterback and I think it bleeds into everybody else too.” “That’s the most important thing, protecting the ball. It’s the number really in our organization. We were moving the ball, we got to protect the ball through and through, and starts with me at quarterback.” Brock Purdy takes responsibility for the 49ers struggles on offense. https://t.co/NklpPIbpbL — 95.7 The Game (@957thegame) October 25, 2026 Looking at the 49ers Purdy finished the game completing 27-of-40 passes for 288 yards, one touchdown, and the two INTs. As a team, the 49ers rushed for 123 yards, so they were able to move the ball but couldn’t capitalize at the end of drives. That ultimately came back to haunt them down the stretch. Tight end George Kittle and running back Christian McCaffrey led all players in receiving yards. Kittle had eight receptions for 88 yards, while McCaffrey recorded six receptions for 61 yards. San Francisco was extremely shorthanded at wide receiver entering the game, and it showed. Without Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel, along with several other players on IR, the team had just four active wide receivers for the matchup. Those four combined for just seven catches. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post 49ers QB Brock Purdy Drops Honest Quote After Loss to Falcons appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Luka Doncic Makes NBA History in 50-Point Game in Lakers-Magic
item.description: When the Los Angeles Lakers were down 18 points against the Utah Jazz on Sunday night, it looked like they were about to suffer their first loss of the season. Instead, Luka Doncic decided to prove why he's one of the best players in the NBA and put up an incredible stat line of 52 points, 10 assists, and 8 rebounds on 57/44/91 shooting from the field. Doncic's performance was so good, he made history in a plethora of ways. Luka Doncic Makes NBA History vs. Magic After Sunday night, Luka Doncic officially became the fastest point guard in NBA history to reach ten different instances of 50-point games. Not only that, but he also now has the most games ever by a point guard of putting up 50+ points and 10+ assists. Doncic's accomplishments extend even further beyond that as well; he also passed Wilt Chamberlain and Shaquille O'Neal in all-time 50-point games for the Lakers. That fact in itself is even more astounding when considering that Doncic has only been a Laker since February of 2025. Rob Gray-Imagn Images That stat alone, speaks volumes to just how prolific of a scorer Luka Doncic truly is. How Good Has Luka Doncic Been This Season? Scary enough, Luka Doncic has been struggling to start the season. While he has moments of being an offensive powerhouse, as he was against the Utah Jazz, his first two games of the season weren't stellar performances. However, with his most recent historic game against the Jazz, Doncic's averages have already changed drastically. After Sunday night, Doncic is now averaging 34.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 8.0 assists on 46/40/89 shooting from the field. Rob Gray-Imagn Images The biggest concern right now is that Luka Doncic is averaging 7 turnovers again, totaling 21 of them through three games. He only had four against the Utah Jazz, which is a huge sigh of relief, but he's been racking them up over the past three games. The most positive piece of insight in all of this is that even though Luka was subpar in his first two games of the season, the Los Angeles Lakers are 3-0 this season. The Lakers are a total team, where multiple members of the roster can pull each other up on a bad night. When Luka was having an off night against the Warriors or Clippers, players like Walker Kessler were able to lift him up. On Sunday night, when Kessler was having a horrible night, Doncic was able to have a historic night and lift his team to a win. At the end of the day, Luka Doncic is the leader of the Lakers, and what he did on Sunday night is the perfect example of why.

item.title: Thunder’s Cason Wallace Update Adds Insult to Jalen Williams Injury
item.description: OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA - OCTOBER 25: Cason Wallace #22 of the Oklahoma City Thunder goes up for a shot during the first half against the LA Clippers at Paycom Center on October 25, 2026 in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Joshua Gateley/Getty Images) Getty The Oklahoma City Thunder had to watch the painful reality of Jalen Williams getting carted off late in Sunday’s game. That wasn’t their first injury trouble of the night, though. Both Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams had already left the game hurt, too. The Thunder went on to beat the Los Angeles Clippers anyway by a 108-101 score. Oklahoma City is now 3-0 on the season. But this is the kind of painful night that can really set a team back. What Happened to Cason Wallace? Wallace was hurt attempting to go through a screen in the first quarter. He appeared to injure his left shoulder, which gave the visual impression of potentially being dislocated. Wallace didn’t come back into the game after the first quarter. What Happened to Jaylin Williams? The other Williams on the Thunder hurt his hand early in the game. He, like Wallace, didn’t play beyond the early stages of Sunday’s game. OKC Thunder Injury Update Thunder coach Mark Daigneault basically said that the Thunder would provide more information on these absences on Monday. This is what beat writer Brandon Rahbar shared on X after the game: Mark Daigneault was asked if there’s any updates on the JDub, JWill and Cason Wallace injuries tonight: “No updates. Obviously Jalen, that one speaks for itself.” Daigneault says that as far as Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams, the team will update tomorrow. — Brandon Rahbar (@BrandonRahbar) October 26, 2026 Who Gets More Minutes? The injury to Jalen Williams happened late on Sunday, so there wasn’t much time to see how the Thunder adjusted to that. But with Wallace and Jaylin Williams both leaving early, there are some hints on the stat sheet. Three bench players got more than 20 minutes: Ajay Mitchell , Alex Caruso and Jared McCain. The Thunder then gave rookie center Aday Mara 14 minutes, and Kenrich Williams also got seven minutes on the inside. And in the interests of more potential point guard playing time being available, rookie Bennett Stirtz got 11 minutes on Sunday night. It’s not great timing for the Thunder to have all these injuries, because they’ve got a back-to-back to complete on Monday night at home against the Phoenix Suns . That does mean, though, that OKC can’t hide from injury realities for long. They’ll have to share some updates sooner rather than later. Even if Jalen Williams is out for a while, the Thunder will be hoping Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams are doing a bit better themselves. This is what beat writer Brandon Rahbar shared on X after the game: Mark Daigneault was asked if there’s any updates on the JDub, JWill and Cason Wallace injuries tonight: “No updates. Obviously Jalen, that one speaks for itself.” Daigneault says that as far as Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams, the team will update tomorrow. — Brandon Rahbar (@BrandonRahbar) October 26, 2026 Who Gets More Minutes? The injury to Jalen Williams happened late on Sunday, so there wasn’t much time to see how the Thunder adjusted to that. But with Wallace and Jaylin Williams both leaving early, there are some hints on the stat sheet. Three bench players got more than 20 minutes: Ajay Mitchell , Alex Caruso and Jared McCain. The Thunder then gave rookie center Aday Mara 14 minutes, and Kenrich Williams also got seven minutes on the inside. And in the interests of more potential point guard playing time being available, rookie Bennett Stirtz got 11 minutes on Sunday night. It’s not great timing for the Thunder to have all these injuries, because they’ve got a back-to-back to complete on Monday night at home against the Phoenix Suns . That does mean, though, that OKC can’t hide from injury realities for long. They’ll have to share some updates sooner rather than later. Even if Jalen Williams is out for a while, the Thunder will be hoping Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams are doing a bit better themselves. item.title: NASCAR Driver Leaves Talladega With Arm in Cast After Terrifying Wreck
item.description: RICHMOND, VIRGINIA - AUGUST 15: Riley Herbst, driver of the #35 Monster Energy Toyota, drives during the NASCAR Cup Series Cook Out 400 at Richmond Raceway on August 15, 2026 in Richmond, Virginia. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) Getty Riley Herbst walked away from one of the most frightening crashes of Sunday’s NASCAR Cup Series race at Talladega Superspeedway. But he wasn’t leaving the track completely unscathed. Hours after his No. 35 Toyota slammed into the inside wall during a massive late-race wreck, Herbst was spotted in the garage area with his left wrist and forearm heavily wrapped and supported. Photos shared by NASCAR reporters showed the 23XI Racing driver speaking with media members and inspecting his damaged car after being released from the infield care center. Despite the alarming images, Herbst offered an encouraging update on his condition, along with a little humor. Riley Herbst Speaks Out After Violent Talladega Crash Herbst was among several drivers caught in a multicar accident with five laps remaining in Sunday’s YellaWood 500. The wreck sent Joey Logano’s No. 22 Ford flipping onto its roof , while Herbst suffered an especially brutal impact against the inside SAFER barrier. The collision was severe enough to interrupt the broadcast feed from Herbst’s in-car camera, adding to concerns as safety workers responded. Herbst eventually climbed from his damaged Toyota with assistance and walked to a waiting safety vehicle. NASCAR subsequently confirmed that Herbst had been evaluated and released from the infield care center. Herbst Offers Encouraging Update Despite Arm Injury Following the race, Herbst was photographed wearing a substantial wrap around his left wrist and forearm. Speaking with USA Sports, Herbst offered a memorable response when asked about his condition. “My dad always said, if you are going to be dumb, be tough. So, cheers.” The remark provided some welcome levity after an accident that had left viewers fearing the worst. Herbst was also seen examining his wrecked race car in the garage, an encouraging sight following the violent impact. NASCAR is also taking Herbst’s No. 35 Toyota to its Research and Development Center for further examination following the violent crash. The car sustained extensive damage after striking the inside SAFER barrier, and the additional inspection will give NASCAR an opportunity to study how it performed during the impact. Although he was released from the care center, the extent of his wrist or arm injury has not been publicly confirmed. The wrap visible in postrace photographs does not, by itself, establish whether he suffered a fracture. Herbst’s race ended with a 36th-place finish , but the result was secondary to the news that he was able to walk away and speak with reporters afterward. For a driver who had just experienced one of Talladega’s hardest hits, that was the most important development of the afternoon . This article was originally published on HEAVY The post NAS

item.title: Lions’ Jahmyr Gibbs reveals NSFW reaction to Dan Campbell’s decision vs. Packers
item.description: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) runs against Green Bay Packers cornerback Keisean Nixon (25) during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Lions’ Jahmyr Gibbs reveals NSFW reaction to Dan Campbell’s decision vs. Packers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Dan Campbell and the Detroit Lions played out a familiar scene at Ford Field in Week 7 as a fourth down gamble went awry against the Packers . Campbell explained his two reasons for going for it on a day when the Lions brought home a 20-17 win and Jahmyr Gibbs shared his thoughts on what transpired. Gibbs failed to get the first down , leading to his NSFW take afterward. “I was like, oh s**t,” Gibbs said. “But I mean, we could’ve gotten that. We just had a mis-ID or something…I was surprised, but when I thought about it I was like, ‘Ah, (screw) it,” the Lions running back said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Lions got huge games on offense and defense from its myriad stars including Brian Branch, who reacted to his game-changing interception after the game. Lions kicker Jake Bates has become one of the NFL’s most clutch players, a distinction he backed up against the Packers with the game on the line. Bates hit the winning field goal , sending Ford Field into a state of pandemonium. The Lions’ fourth down gamble didn’t pay off, but it emboldened Campbell’s team at a time when they needed some extra confidence. Campbell said afterward that he felt the Lions would get the ball back at some point, and he was right. Both Detroit and Green Bay were shorthanded with the Lions missing Kerby Joseph and the Packers without Micah Parsons, but good football was played by both sides, and Gibbs was a huge part of it. Related: Why Mike Tomlin believes Lions’ Dan Campbell made right 4th down decision vs. Packers Related: Lions’ Brian Branch reacts to massive INT in injury return

item.title: Chiefs and 49ers suffer first losses of NFL season, Vikings stay unbeaten
item.description: Jessie Bates III of the Atlanta Falcons punches the ball out from George Kittle in the Falcons' NFL victory over the San Francisco 49ers (Todd Kirkland) The Seattle Seahawks put on a defensive masterclass to hand the Kansas City Chiefs their first defeat of the NFL season on Sunday, winning 20-3, while the San Francisco 49ers also surrendered their perfect start to the Atlanta Falcons. Seattle utterly stifled their former running back Kenneth Walker III, who won the Super Bowl last season with the Seahawks and had led the NFL this year with the Chiefs in rushing yards per game ahead of Sunday's clash. He could only manage 36 rushing yards from 14 carries on his return to Lumen Field, as the Seattle defense collectively swarmed their opponents, sacking Patrick Mahomes once and forcing another interception. "We just had the one mindset -- to go in and just disrupt," said Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori, who rushed Mahomes to create a Ty Okada pick that led to a Seattle touchdown on the next drive. The scoreline was the Chiefs' joint-lowest in a game Mahomes started. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught a looping 28-yard pass from Sam Darnold in the second quarter but was initially judged to have run out-of-bounds, before a video review awarded the touchdown. Walker's Seattle replacement Emanuel Wilson rushed 21 yards through a gap at the heart of the Chiefs' defense in the fourth quarter. Harrison Butker missed two field goals on a chastening night for the high-flying Chiefs. Meanwhile in Atlanta, Michael Penix threw for three touchdowns and the Falcons defense forced four turnovers in a 29-20 win over the 49ers. Penix connected with tight end Nick Muse for a touchdown to keep the Falcons within striking distance in the first half and hit Kyle Pitts for a TD that put Atlanta ahead in the third quarter. He found Drake London with a 21-yard touchdown pass in the fourth. "Too sloppy to win," 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said. - 'Proud' - Those results left the Minnesota Vikings as the only remaining unbeaten team, holding the Indianapolis Colts scoreless in the second half in a 16-10 victory that saw them improve to 6-0. Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray threw a five-yard touchdown pass to T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter and Will Reichard kicked a 52-yard field goal with 1:39 remaining. Sunday's action kicked off in Paris, where Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers threw for 212 yards and a milestone touchdown to lead the Steelers to a 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints in the league's first regular-season game in the French capital. Rodgers hit Darnell Washington with a four-yard TD pass to give the Steelers a 10-3 lead late in the second quarter, his 540th regular-season touchdown pass moving him into solo third place on the all-time list ahead of Peyton Manning (539). Harrison Butker missed two field goals on a chastening night for the high-flying Chiefs. Meanwhile in Atlanta, Michael Penix threw for three touchdowns and the Falcons defense forced four turnovers in a 29-20 win over the 49ers. Penix connected with tight end Nick Muse for a touchdown to keep the Falcons within striking distance in the first half and hit Kyle Pitts for a TD that put Atlanta ahead in the third quarter. He found Drake London with a 21-yard touchdown pass in the fourth. "Too sloppy to win," 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said. - 'Proud' - Those results left the Minnesota Vikings as the only remaining unbeaten team, holding the Indianapolis Colts scoreless in the second half in a 16-10 victory that saw them improve to 6-0. Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray threw a five-yard touchdown pass to T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter and Will Reichard kicked a 52-yard field goal with 1:39 remaining. Rodgers hit Darnell Washington with a four-yard TD pass to give the Steelers a 10-3 lead late in the second quarter, his 540th regular-season touchdown pass moving him into solo third place on the all-time list ahead of Peyton Manning (539). The Los Angeles Rams snapped a two-game skid in emphatic style, beating the Raiders 35-21 in Las Vegas. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns, all in the first half. He became the franchise leader in scoring passes -- an honor Stafford also holds with the Detroit Lions. "We've had some tough losses late in games this year, played good enough football to win games and hadn't gotten it done... proud of our resolve," said Stafford. In Houston, Devin Singletary ran 30 yards for a touchdown in overtime to lift the New York Giants to a 27-21 upset win over the Texans. In Detroit, Jake Bates kicked a 22-yard field goal as time expired to give the Lions a 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers. Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes in the second half as the Bengals rallied to beat the Ravens 35-13 in Baltimore. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson piloted his fifth fourth-quarter game-winning drive of the season, capped by Andre Szmyt's 32-yard field goal as time expired in the Browns' 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville. And the Miami Dolphins earned their first win of the season, beating the New York Jets 28-25 in New Jersey. amz-bb/lkd

item.title: Packers’ Xavier McKinney calls out refs in wild NSFW rant after loss to Lions
item.description: Tork Mason/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin Packers’ Xavier McKinney calls out refs in wild NSFW rant after loss to Lions appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Green Bay Packers were on the wrong end of a controversial roughing the passer call late in their 20-17 loss to the Detroit Lions. That penalty was a costly one as it helped the Lions kick their last-second field goal to win the game. That was one of two iffy penalties called against the Packers in the game, to the dismay of their defense stars. Packers pass rusher Micah Parsons already bashed the referees and the NFL on social media . And after the game, safety Xavier McKinney also called out the officials for those questionable calls , while using some colorful language. “I don’t know how the NFL’s going to treat it, but I’m not a big fan of the refs right now,” McKinney said. “I don’t think it’s great officiating, if I’m being completely honest. I think it’s bulls— a lot of the times.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the Packers were on the receiving side of some dubious calls, they also didn’t help themselves against the Lions. Kicker Trey Smack missed two of his three field goal attempts, including a potential go-ahead field goal in the fourth quarter that was blocked. Meanwhile, Packers quarterback Jordan Love admitted that the offense wasn’t quite at its best . Based on the penalties the Packers were called for, it seems clear the NFL needs to look at how roughing the passer is being judged. At the moment, there is a disconnect with the referees and the players and fans. At the same time, though, the Packers will need to set aside their frustrations with the refs and focus on what they can control moving forward. Related: 3 Packers most to blame for letting crucial game vs. Lions slip away Related: Packers’ Josh Jacobs apologizes to team after crucial blunder in loss to Lions

item.title: Xabi Alonso: ‘We have to be critical of ourselves’

An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. / | AFP via Getty Images I needed a solid 24-36 hours of absolute Chelsea-detox after that horrendous defeat on Saturday. The history of the fixture is one thing — only the second win for Spurs at the Bridge since 1990 — but combined with the performance, the approach, and the attitude shown throughout … and, yeah, we needed to be on a break for a minute. But while time may heal some wounds, this one still stings. There were many mistakes made this weekend. Some were obvious. Some were less so. And I’d argue it was the less obvious ones that truly doomed us. Unfortunately, no one bothered to ask manager Xabi Alonso about those. “We can do better and we have to be critical of ourselves.” -Xabi Alonso; source: Chelsea FC Mike Penders sliced a one-fisted punch straight into the back of his own net — I don’t think I’ve ever seen that before; and probably will never see something like that again! — and that broke the team. Cole Palmer’s red card, questionable or not, just made sure of it. “I had the feeling that it was going to be about the first goal, the second half it was being tight, some half chances from them, some half chances from us, it was going to be about the key moment and once we have conceded the first goal it has changed everything. Straight away almost when we wanted to have a reaction, the red card and it went the other way and probably we can do better, so it is one to reflect in this big game that it was and it is a good opponent, the performance is one to improve.” -Xabi Alonso; source: Football.London But the team broke because of the decisions that were made, and then not made, prior to any of those events happening. It broke because of the setup, because of the approach (individual and collective), and because of the reactions (individual and collective). João Pedro’s injury in training obviously caused a last-minute rethink, but whatever it was that Alonso came up with was not the correct answer. More damningly, his unwillingness (or inability) to change things during the game was quite alarming. All game we had Morgan Rogers trying to hold up long balls from the back. All game we had 2-v-3 in the center of the pitch and were constantly exposed. The defense was a mess, trying to cover the extra man in midfield. Marco Palestra was used in a defensive role and on the wrong flank; Geovany Quenda bombed on his full debut, which somehow lasted 72 minutes. If the plan is to not be on the front-foot, then the plan has to be more reactive. “We win, we lose together and it is part of the job to deal with and to overcome from mistakes, myself as well and everyone … [we] have to show that we can do better” -Xabi Alonso; source: Football.London And we’ll have to show that very quickly. Liverpool in the League Cup midweek is a bit of a bonus game, win or lose, but an absolutely horrendous Manchester United at home next weekend is now even more of a must-win game.

item.title: Did Jakob Poeltl Play Tonight? Why Raptors’ Center Scored 0 Points
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Jakob Poeltl #19 of the Toronto Raptors and Rudy Gobert #27 of the Minnesota Timberwolves compete for the rebound in the first quarter during the home opener at Target Center on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Getty The Toronto Raptors lost in blowout fashion to the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday. Things got off to a bad start before the ball was even tossed, because the Raptors learned soon before the game that they’d have to play without Kawhi Leonard. But it’s not like Toronto put up much of a fight once the game began, either. Two of their five starters were held scoreless. One of those was Scottie Barnes, an incredible shock you can read more about here. The other was Jakob Poeltl , the experienced center. He didn’t score for the entirety of Sunday’s game. Did Jakob Poeltl Play Tonight? Yes, Jakob Poeltl was active, healthy and on the floor for the Raptors on Sunday night. Despite that, he didn’t score a single point. The Raptors have continued to use Poeltl in the starting lineup over the likes of Collin Murray-Boyles and Trayce Jackson-Davis , but it’s not working out for Toronto at the moment. Jakob Poeltl Stats Poeltl ended up playing 19 minutes in Sunday’s game for the Raptors. Despite that, he didn’t score. Poeltl only attempted two field goals and missed them both. He also had just one rebound. Poeltel turned the ball over once and was a minus-18. It’s actually astounding that he attempted two shots, didn’t score and grabbed just one rebound with no defensive stats in 19 minutes. Why Jakob Poeltl Scored 0 Points The most obvious reality for Poeltl is that he hardly shot. Just two shot attempts in 19 minutes, and not making it to the foul line, really limits the offensive upside. Poeltl isn’t meant to lead the Raptors’ offense, but that’s still a really tough showing. The other obvious point is that the Timberwolves start Rudy Gobert at center. Even as he ages, Gobert remains one of the top defenders of this generation. Against a slower and plodding center like Poeltl, one who doesn’t shoot it from the outside, Gobert is well-equipped to dominate. Poeltl is never going to score a lot of points, but any night he faces a center like Gobert will be even tougher. The Raptors had won their first two games of the season, so now they’ve fallen to 2-1 while the Wolves move to 3-0. For Toronto to bounce back the next time out, they’ll need a bit more scoring and rebounding production from the center position. item.content:encoded: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Jakob Poeltl #19 of the Toronto Raptors and Rudy Gobert #27 of the Minnesota Timberwolves compete for the rebound in the first quarter during the home opener at Target Center on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Getty The Toronto Raptors lost in blowout fashion to the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday. Things got off to a bad start before the ball was even tossed, because the Raptors learned soon before the game that they’d have to play without Kawhi Leonard. But it’s not like Toronto put up much of a fight once the game began, either. Two of their five starters were held scoreless. One of those was Scottie Barnes, an incredible shock you can read more about here. The other was Jakob Poeltl , the experienced center. He didn’t score for the entirety of Sunday’s game. Did Jakob Poeltl Play Tonight? Yes, Jakob Poeltl was active, healthy and on the floor for the Raptors on Sunday night. Despite that, he didn’t score a single point. The Raptors have continued to use Poeltl in the starting lineup over the likes of Collin Murray-Boyles and Trayce Jackson-Davis , but it’s not working out for Toronto at the moment. Jakob Poeltl Stats Poeltl ended up playing 19 minutes in Sunday’s game for the Raptors. Despite that, he didn’t score. Poeltl only attempted two field goals and missed them both. He also had just one rebound. Poeltel turned the ball over once and was a minus-18. It’s actually astounding that he attempted two shots, didn’t score and grabbed just one rebound with no defensive stats in 19 minutes. Why Jakob Poeltl Scored 0 Points The most obvious reality for Poeltl is that he hardly shot. Just two shot attempts in 19 minutes, and not making it to the foul line, really limits the offensive upside. Poeltl isn’t meant to lead the Raptors’ offense, but that’s still a really tough showing. The other obvious point is that the Timberwolves start Rudy Gobert at center. Even as he ages, Gobert remains one of the top defenders of this generation. Against a slower and plodding center like Poeltl, one who doesn’t shoot it from the outside, Gobert is well-equipped to dominate. Poeltl is never going to score a lot of points, but any night he faces a center like Gobert will be even tougher. The Raptors had won their first two games of the season, so now they’ve fallen to 2-1 while the Wolves move to 3-0. For Toronto to bounce back the next time out, they’ll need a bit more scoring and rebounding production from the center position. Those feeling compelled to spend some time on the couch should heed this warning. The North American sporting calendar is often sequestered, with leagues whose seasons start in the spring or summer giving way around this point to those who get their strength in the autumn and winter. That is an imperfect science, though. For a few glorious days, an eclipse can happen — a day where each matchup that takes hold of one league's calendar is swallowed up by a corresponding fixture in a different competition. This year, the sports equinox will fall upon Monday night. Onlookers should be ready to make arrangements to follow along with the action. The Rays will attempt to capitalize on their frightful pitching, with Freddy Peralta slated to take the bump on Monday. He'll get quite the test in a talent-laden Brewers lineup spearheaded by William Contreras, Jackson Chourio, Brice Turang and Jake Bauers. NBA Game Time (ET) TV/Live stream Wizards vs. Hornets 7 p.m. DAZN (Wizards), DAZN (Hornets) ITimberwolves vs. Cavaliers 7 p.m. DAZN (Timberwolves), DAZN (Cavaliers) Bulls vs. Celtics 7:30 p.m. — Mavericks vs. Heat 7:30 p.m. NBA TV, fubo , DIRECTV Pacers vs. Bucks 8 p.m. DAZN (Pacers) Suns vs. Thunder 8 p.m. — Hawks vs. Rockets 8:30 p.m. — Grizzlies vs. Jazz 9 p.m. DAZN (Grizzlies) Warriors vs. Nuggets 10 p.m. NBC Sports Network, Peacock , fubo , DIRECTV The WNBA isn't the only basketball competition slated to take center stage during the sports equinox. Dybantsa could make his regular-season debut in Washington's tilt with the Hornets, while the Timberwolves and Cavaliers will look to cement their status as some of their respective conference's truest heavyweight. NHL Game Time (ET) TV/Live stream Kings vs. Rangers 7 p.m. NHL Network, DAZN (Kings), DAZN (Rangers), fubo , DIRECTV Maple Leafs vs. Flames 8:30 p.m. ESPN+ Red Wings vs. Oilers 9:30 p.m. ESPN+ Lastly, we have a three-game NHL slate to munch down on during the sports equinox. Six sides play in total, including the Western Conference-leading Edmonton Oilers, anchored by magician Connor McDavid. The 29-year-old entered Friday with 31 points (eight goals, 23 assists) in 10 games — good for an average of 3.1 points per match. He'll put his glittering scoring record to the test against the Red Wings, a side attempting to find relevancy after a dour start to the campaign.

item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Sid Lowe at the Camp Nou
item.content:encoded: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin
item.description: Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under the current leadership and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too well Dropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone. Carrick said the decision to drop the Portuguese playmaker was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after the desperate defeat to Como cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s comments on the lack of pressing in the Champions League fixture. It was somewhat telling that Lisandro Martínez kept his place despite pointing out the director of football, Jason Wilcox, was a hindrance to the club the previous week. Continue reading...

After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break. item.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
item.description: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile. There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. Continue reading...

item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.description: Lazio win 2-1 while Roma draw 3-3 with Napoli Beier gives Dortmund win over Eintracht Frankfurt Lazio climbed to the top of Serie A with a 2-1 home win ⁠over Parma ⁠as Roma ​twice came from behind to secure a 3-3 draw with Napoli in a pulsating clash in Naples. Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this ⁠season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor ⁠struck his first of the season, before Parma’s Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying ​to cut out a cross. item.description: Home side broke the game open with some unique corner routines, but a goalkeeping error ruined the plan There was an odd interlude at Stamford Bridge with 76 minutes gone and the score still 0-0, one of those moments where suddenly your brain seems to be on inside out, like trying to walk the wrong way down an escalator. Tottenham had a corner on the left-hand side, in a game that had felt to that point like an extended practice session, a refinement of systems, the football equivalent of watching two middle-aged men methodically emptying the dishwasher, adding salt, descaling the hoses, tutting over knives incorrectly slotted, cups in the wrong row. item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. Continue reading...

item.title: Championship roundup: Southampton beat West Ham; QPR put five past Swansea
item.description: Hammers humbled at home; Swansea thrashed 5-0 Burnley sack manager Hayen after 4-1 loss at Lincoln Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham . Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin were all on target in a chaotic first half, while Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers. Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. Southampton, deducted four points at the start of the season, are now just two points behind West Ham. Continue reading...

The Belgian was appointed in the summer as the permanent successor to Scott Parker, who left in April with relegation from the Premier League inevitable. He leaves having won just one match, a 4-0 league victory at Watford on 10 October. Continue reading...

item.title: Maresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless start
item.description: Defender costs three goals in past two league matches Emery praises ‘fantastic’ match-winner Jackson Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season. Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend. Continue reading...

item.title: Nicolas Jackson double sees Aston Villa end Manchester City’s perfect start
item.description: Manchester City added a loss in the Premier League to one to the Premier League, as their perfect record this season vanished without an independent commission in sight. Two of the most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side came out on top against Erling Haaland. City are certainly fallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games. Mistakes cost City as Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma were punished by Jackson, who will have taken great pleasure in ending the winning run of his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca. Continue reading...

Mistakes cost City as Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma were punished by Jackson, who will have taken great pleasure in ending the winning run of his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

It has been difficult, gruelling in parts, but also warm, exhilarating and at times deeply erotic. Yes. I was SAVAGED by Simon Jordan. And I’ve never felt so alive. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
